text:
Everyone is watching one man step down, and allegations still unproven in court. A friend in the industry told me something else. This is his account. I have not verified it. It is not established fact.

He said that 128 GB300 units, recently out of Hsinchu, are being offered for rent in Shenzhen — on five-year contracts. Five years, he added, is normal now.

A few months ago, he was taken to sit in on a Shenzhen group that flips Nvidia GPUs and overseas data centers. People in that role, he said, are not rare. I will not name anyone. The system is still running.

His read is that Nvidia needs cash from GPUs that actually get sold, he said, because many of the GPUs are being financed by the supply chain. If that is right, Taiwan's vendors carry the cash and the compliance risk: the rental desk is in Shenzhen, and the financing sits here.

These people, he said, now stay ahead of U.S. tracking. Over the past year they have been buying Japanese data-center companies that can pass U.S. review. Washington chases where the chips go. They buy compute that can clear review.

The gray market is not a secret. International reports this year already had high-end AI servers trading at multiples of list price on the mainland, often via Hong Kong and Shenzhen, and Washington is debating rules on remote access to overseas data centers. My friend was more specific: the new route, he said, runs through Japan.

Two questions.

Chips iterate this fast, and you sign a five-year contract — what do you do with the hardware in year five, barbecue on it?

And further out: in five years, can anyone even bet that Taiwan will still be speaking with one voice?

The real story is not one man's private life, or one CEO chair. It is a gray-market ecosystem that knows how to move — from Shenzhen rentals and supply-chain financing, to "review-ready" compute in Japan. For Taiwan, and for export control, that is bigger than the scandal headlines.

The allegations remain unproven in court. A man can step down. If this channel is still open, the fire still gets carried out the back door. Next time, there may be no one left to walk into Washington and speak for Taiwan.

text:
Overview of the World Bank Group

The World Bank Group is a collection of five international organizations that provide financial and technical assistance to developing countries. Its primary goals are to reduce poverty and promote sustainable development.
Key Institutions
The World Bank Group consists of the following institutions:

Institution

International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)

Provides loans and financial services to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries.

International Development Association (IDA)

Offers concessional loans and grants to the poorest countries.
International Finance Corporation (IFC)

Supports private sector development by providing investment and advisory services.
Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA)

Provides political risk insurance and credit enhancement to encourage foreign investment.
International Centre for the Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID)

Facilitates the resolution of investment disputes between governments and foreign investors.

Mission and Goals

The World Bank Group aims to achieve the following:

End Extreme Poverty: 
Focus on reducing the number of people living on less than $1.90 a day.

Promote Shared Prosperity: Enhance the living standards of the poorest 40% of the population in developing countries.

Headquarters and Membership
Location: 

The World Bank Group is headquartered in Washington, D.C.

Membership: It has 189 member countries, which include both donor and borrowing nations.

The World Bank Group plays a crucial role in addressing global development challenges and fostering economic growth in developing regions.

text:
Joseph Smith’s “Most Correct” Claim and The Evidence

The Book of Mormon makes a set of bold theological claims. It says that important parts of the gospel were removed from the Bible and that it restores them (1 Nephi 13:26-29, 40).

It describes the resurrected Jesus appearing to people in the Americas, organizing a church, and teaching the fulness of the gospel there (3 Nephi 11-28). These are not presented as symbols or later interpretations. They are offered as real historical events. For those claims to stand, the Book of Mormon must be what it says it is: an accurate ancient record translated by the gift and power of God.

Joseph Smith reinforced that premise. On November 28, 1841 he told associates that the Book of Mormon was "the most correct of any book on earth" (History of the Church 4:461). By that date he had already revised the text for two earlier editions.

The changes were not trivial. Hundreds of grammatical corrections were made, and specific wording was altered. In several places in 1 Nephi 11 the 1830 edition said "mother of God." The 1837 edition, prepared under Smith's direction, changed the phrase to "mother of the Son of God" (Royal Skousen, Analysis of Textual Variants of the Book of Mormon; Joseph Smith Papers, 1830 and 1837 Book of Mormon editions).

The same pattern of adjustment appears in a central historical claim. The official introduction to the 1981 edition stated that the Lamanites "are the principal ancestors of the American Indians." That wording matched how Joseph Smith and early leaders had spoken about Native Americans.

Starting in 2006 the introduction was changed to say the Lamanites are "among the ancestors of the American Indians" (comparison of the 1981 and 2006 official editions). The Church's Gospel Topics essay "Book of Mormon and DNA Studies" (2014, https://t.co/N5AC9fRBrC) notes that the majority of Native American DNA most closely matches eastern Asian populations and that genetics cannot decisively confirm the Book of Mormon’s historical claims.

The text's own details face the same problem. Alma 18:9-12 describes horses being prepared along with chariots so a king could travel. Horses became extinct in the Americas by the end of the Pleistocene and returned only with European contact (David J. Meltzer, First Peoples in a New World: Populating Ice Age America, 2nd edition, 2021).

No pre-Columbian remains of horses used with wheeled vehicles for transport have been found (Michael D. Coe and Stephen Houston, The Maya, 9th edition, 2015). Small ceramic wheeled figurines exist in the Remojadas tradition of Veracruz but are toys or ritual objects, not chariots (Coe and Houston, The Maya, 9th edition). 

References to steel tools and weapons appear in 2 Nephi 5:15 and Jarom 1:8, yet no evidence of pre-Columbian steel production matching those descriptions has been identified in the relevant regions (Dorothy Hosler, The Sounds and Colors of Power: The Sacred Metallurgical Technology of Ancient West Mexico, 1994). No inscriptions naming the Book of Mormon's peoples have been recovered.

Genetic findings point in the same direction. Ancient DNA studies show that the ancestors of Native Americans derive primarily from Northeast Asian populations, with the main migrations occurring well before 600 BC (David Reich, Who We Are and How We Got Here, 2018; Pontus Skoglund et al., "Genetic Evidence for Two Founding Populations of the Americas," Nature, volume 525, 2015).

There is no clear genetic signal of large-scale Middle Eastern migrations of the kind required by the traditional reading. The Church's 2014 Gospel Topics essay acknowledges this data.

Taken together, the revisions Joseph Smith made, the later official change in the ancestry statement, and the absence of the archaeological and genetic evidence the narrative requires remove the historical foundation the book's theological claims depend on. The 1841 Smith declaration that the Book of Mormon is the most correct book on earth does not hold up against the documented record.

Joseph Smith claimed an angel delivered an ancient record and that he restored the fulness of the gospel, declaring the Book of Mormon the most correct book on earth. The revisions he made, the official retreat from the Lamanite ancestry claim, and the absence of confirming archaeological and genetic evidence show those claims failed.

Galatians 1:8-9 states: “But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed. As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.”

By that standard he was a false prophet.

text:
Joy Buolamwini, the renowned AI researcher and activist, appears on the Zoom screen from home in Boston, wearing her signature thick-rimmed glasses. 

As an MIT grad, she seems genuinely interested in seeing old covers of MIT Technology Review that hang in our London office. An edition of the magazine from 1961 asks: “Will your son get into college?” 

I can tell Buolamwini finds the cover amusing. She takes a picture of it. Times have changed a lot since 1961. In her new memoir, Unmasking AI: My Mission to Protect What Is Human in a World of Machines, Buolamwini shares her life story. In many ways she embodies how far tech has come since then, and how much further it still needs to go. 

Buolamwini is best known for a pioneering paper she co-wrote with AI researcher Timnit Gebru in 2018, called “Gender Shades,” which exposed how commercial facial recognition systems often failed to recognize the faces of Black and brown people, especially Black women. Her research and advocacy led companies such as Google, IBM, and Microsoft to improve their software so it would be less biased and back away from selling their technology to law enforcement. 

Now, Buolamwini has a new target in sight. She is calling for a radical rethink of how AI systems are built. Buolamwini tells MIT Technology Review that, amid the current AI hype cycle, she sees a very real risk of letting technology companies pen the rules that apply to them—repeating the very mistake, she argues, that has previously allowed biased and oppressive technology to thrive.

“What concerns me is we’re giving so many companies a free pass, or we’re applauding the innovation while turning our head [away from the harms],” Buolamwini says. 

A particular concern, says Buolamwini, is the basis upon which we are building today’s sparkliest AI toys, so-called foundation models. Technologists envision these multifunctional models serving as a springboard for many other AI applications, from chatbots to automated movie-making. They are built by scraping masses of data from the internet, inevitably including copyrighted content and personal information. Many AI companies are now being sued by artists, music companies, and writers, who claim their intellectual property was taken without consent. 

The current modus operandi of today’s AI companies is unethical—a form of “data colonialism,” Buolamwini says, with a “full disregard for consent.”  

“What’s out there for the taking, if there aren’t laws—it’s just pillaged,” she says. As an author, Buolamwini says, she fully expects her book, her poems, her voice, and her op-eds—even her PhD dissertation—to be scraped into AI models. 

“Should I find that any of my work has been used in these systems, I will definitely speak up. That’s what we do,” she says.  

Buolamwini says a real innovation worth boasting about would be models that companies could show have a positive climate impact and legitimately sourced data, for example. 

“I see an opportunity to learn from so many mistakes of the past when it comes to oppressive systems powering advanced technologies. My hope is we go in a different direction,” she says.

I ask what aspect of AI systems she would audit today if she could repeat the success of “Gender Shades.” Without missing a beat, Buolamwini says that instead of one single audit, she would like AI to have an audit culture, where systems get rigorously tested before they are deployed in the real world. She’d like to see AI developers ask essential questions about any system they come up with, such as: How does it do what it does, and should we even be using it? 

“Right now we’re in guinea pig mode, where the systems haven’t been fully tested … That’s irresponsible, especially when these systems are being used in ways that impact people’s lived experiences and life opportunities,” she says. 

An accidental activist

Buolamwini has been at the forefront of raising awareness around AI harms for the better part of a decade. But her path to becoming a prominent researcher and activist was far from typical. 

Her memoir gives us an inside look into how she evolved from a young computer science student who didn’t want to deal with “consequences and humans,” as she puts it, into someone who could not look away when confronted with deeply flawed technology that she realized was not created for people like her. 

In a striking moment in the book, she describes discovering that common facial recognition software would recognize a white Halloween mask but not her own face. Although she was unsettled, Buolamwini’s initial reaction was that someone else, perhaps a more seasoned AI researcher, would take care of the problem. But the more examples she saw of algorithmic bias, the harder it became not to do something herself. 

While still a PhD researcher, propelled by the findings of her research on facial recognition, Buolamwini founded the Algorithmic Justice League (AJL), a nonprofit organization fighting algorithmic biases and injustice, and became a prominent voice warning about the harm posed by biased AI systems. In 2019, she gave a pair of expert testimonies to Congress on facial recognition technology and its effect on civil rights and liberties.

While Buolamwini’s story is in some ways inspirational, it’s also a warning. The pressure of raising awareness about AI harms and speaking up against some of the world’s most powerful companies took a toll. In a particularly sad and touching part of the book, Buolamwini describes checking herself into an emergency room the night before an exam, exhausted from the stress of back-to-back congressional testimonies on top of extensive travel and advocacy. 

After she’d done years of intense work setting up the AJL and advising governments about AI while working on her PhD, her “burnout mode” was so overwhelming that in 2021, she wrote a letter to her professors, saying she might drop out. She asked them to make a case for the actual benefit of an MIT PhD—which would be her fourth university degree. 

She took a month off from writing her dissertation to rest, and took up skateboarding. “Maybe it was not too late to become a professional skateboarder and maybe even represent Ghana at the next Olympics,” Buolamwini writes, tongue in cheek. 

In the end, she decided to finish her doctorate, graduating in 2022. She resolved to do so, she writes, after realizing that for her as a woman of color, unlike white colleagues, dropping out of a degree program would be seen as a failure. 

Big risk, big reward

Buolamwini also describes an episode in which she went up against a tech “Goliath,” Amazon. Her PhD research about auditing facial recognition systems elicited public attacks from senior executives at the company, which was at the time—in 2019—competing with Microsoft for a $10 billion contract to provide AI services to the Pentagon. After research by Buolamwini and Inioluwa Deborah Raji, another AI researcher, showed that Amazon’s facial recognition technology was biased, an Amazon vice president, Matt Wood, claimed that her paper and press coverage about it were “misleading” and drew “false conclusions.” 

Amazon was the only technology company that took a combative approach to Buolamwini’s research, she says. She worried she’d put Raji, who at the time was still an undergraduate, in danger: “Prospective computer science departments might perceive her as too much of a risk. Future employers in the tech industry could blacklist her,” Buolamwini writes. 

“I was concerned that if other researchers saw what Amazon was doing to us and no academics stood up in defense, other researchers would perceive the professional risk of this kind of research as being too high,” Buolamwini adds. 

Many people came to fight in her corner. The American Civil Liberties Union of Massachusetts and the Georgetown Law Center on Privacy and Technology supported her publicly on Twitter (now X). In the research community, Margaret Mitchell and Gebru, who at the time were leading Google’s AI ethics work, organized an open letter in support of Buolamwini’s work. Seventy-five researchers, including Turing Prize winner Yoshua Bengio, signed it. 

Disappointingly, she says, most of the public support she received was from outside MIT. In her book, she writes that she felt she had been “largely abandoned by the majority of MIT leadership at that moment.” 

“I assumed the Media Lab, which showcased my work to attract students and news coverage, would defend me. It was disappointing to feel like I had to plead for protection and then receive very little,” Buolamwini writes. (We have contacted MIT Media Lab for comment on this allegation, and will update this piece if they reply.)

Her advice to young people in tech who want to speak up about the problems they see? “Don’t jump in the deep end not knowing that it’s deep,” Buolamwini says. She wants more people to be able to call it out when they see injustices. 

But at the same time, she advises them to surround themselves with people who can offer support and protection. “Your voice matters,” she says.

Correction: A previous version of this story stated incorrectly the year “Gender Shades” was published. It has now been corrected. We apologize for any inconvenience.

O'Keefe v Read et al Wrongful Death suit

Waterfall Bar & Grill has officially joined C.F. McCarthy's motion seeking to exclude the expert report and testimony of Dr. Marissa Orlowski, the hospitality expert retained by the plaintiffs.

Both establishments are now challenging the admissibility of her opinions.

🔶 1. WATERFALL ADOPTS C.F. McCARTHY'S LEGAL ARGUMENTS.

 Waterfall adopts Sections I–III of C.F. McCarthy's motion and accompanying memorandum, to the extent those arguments apply to Orlowski's opinions concerning Waterfall.

Rather than submitting an entirely separate analysis, Waterfall is aligning itself with McCarthy's effort to keep Orlowski's opinions out of the case.

🔶 2. THE DEFENSE CHALLENGES THE USE OF BAR OPERATING PRACTICES TO ESTABLISH INTOXICATION.

Waterfall argues that Orlowski's opinions concerning a bar's "mode of operation" are irrelevant to the legal standard governing Massachusetts dram shop cases.

Its position is that criticisms of an establishment's policies, procedures, or alcohol-service practices cannot substitute for legally sufficient evidence that a patron was visibly intoxicated.

Waterfall cites several decisions supporting its argument, including:

🔷 Homan v. Brandy Barrel Pub & Grill

🔷 Phoung Luc v. Wyndham Management Corp.

🔷 Felt Enterprises v. Chau Chow II

🔶 3. WATERFALL DIRECTLY CHALLENGES ORLOWSKI'S QUALIFICATIONS.

This is one of the more significant arguments in the filing.

Waterfall contends that reviewing Orlowski's credentials and report demonstrates she is not qualified to determine whether someone was visibly intoxicated or had a particular blood alcohol concentration based on surveillance footage.

The defense cites Commonwealth v. Lanigan and Abdulky v. Lubin & Meyer in support of its challenge.

Essentially, Waterfall is questioning whether her hospitality expertise provides a reliable foundation for the specific conclusions she offers.

🔶 4. WATERFALL WANTS HER REPORT AND TESTIMONY EXCLUDED ENTIRELY.

The establishment is asking the court to:

🔷Strike Orlowski's expert report.

🔷 Refuse to consider her report during summary judgment proceedings.

🔷 Exclude her from offering expert opinions or testimony in the case.

WHY THIS MATTERS:

The O'Keefe family is attempting to use Orlowski's expertise to support allegations involving alcohol-service practices and visible intoxication.

But now BOTH establishments named as defendants are challenging whether her opinions should be considered at all.

The plaintiffs argue that her specialized training and experience can help explain how bartenders should recognize intoxication and when intervention is appropriate.

The establishments dispute whether her conclusions meet the legal requirements for admissible expert testimony.

The battle over expert testimony is becoming a significant part of this civil litigation.

C.F. McCarthy's and Waterfall are not simply disputing Orlowski's conclusions. They are asking the court to prevent the plaintiffs from presenting those opinions altogether.

text:
Has there ever been any confirmation or witnesses to the story James Patterson made up about Trump ejecting Epstein from Mara Lago because he hit on a members daughter?

No named first-hand witnesses, the alleged member, or the daughter have ever publicly come forward to confirm the story. While several books and journalists have corroborated that Jeffrey Epstein's Mar-a-Lago membership was closed in October 2007, the exact reason for his removal relies on anonymous sources, secondhand accounts, and shifting explanations from Donald Trump himself. 

What Corroborates the Story

James Patterson’s Filthy Rich (2016): In his non-fiction book about Epstein, Patterson (himself a Mar-a-Lago member) wrote that a fellow member told Trump that Epstein had invited his teenage daughter to his Palm Beach home and tried to get her to undress. Patterson also stated in interviews that he spoke to a former Mar-a-Lago spa manager who claimed she reported Epstein to Trump for making advances toward young girls at the spa, leading Trump to ban him. 

Miami Herald’s The Grifter’s Club (2020): Investigative journalists from the Miami Herald and Wall Street Journal independently reported a similar account. They obtained a Mar-a-Lago membership registry showing Epstein’s account was closed in October 2007—not labeled "Resigned" like most former members. An anonymous Mar-a-Lago member told the authors that Trump kicked Epstein out after he harassed a member's teenage daughter, fearing it would damage the Trump brand.

Statements to Associates: According to The New York Times, Trump privately gave the "member's daughter" explanation to associates. Victims' attorney Brad Edwards also stated that Trump told him a similar story when Edwards interviewed him in 2009. [1, 2]

Contradictions and Disputes

No Named Witnesses: Neither the father, the teenage daughter, nor the former spa manager has ever been publicly named or gone on the record to verify the incident.
Trump’s Changing Explanations: While Trump praised Patterson in 2019 for recounting the ban, Trump has offered conflicting versions over time. He initially claimed Epstein was never a member of the club (which the 2007 registry contradicted) and said their falling out happened around 2004. In July 2025, Trump gave a completely different reason, telling reporters he banned Epstein because Epstein "stole" young female spa employees—specifically naming accuser Virginia Giuffre—to work for him. 

Disputes in Unredacted Files: Following the passage of the Epstein Files Transparency Act, Rep. Maxwell Frost stated in February 2026 that unredacted Department of Justice files he reviewed contained witness statements that directly contradicted Trump's accounts of how and when he expelled Epstein from Mar-a-Lago.

text:
Rao hangs bloated and sluggish above the horizon, less a star than an old coal dying in ash, spilling heavy carmine light across the crystal viaducts of Kandor. Ten million Kryptonians move along suspended glass walkways in robes of gold, cobalt, and viridian, probably assuming tomorrow will look more or less like yesterday. Why shouldn't they? Krypton has stood civilized for a hundred thousand turns.

Inside the Hall of Chronicles, Jor-El stands before a curved quartz projection screen, fingers stained grey with core-drill dust, pleading with seven white-haired magistrates in distant Kryptonopolis who barely bother looking up from their datapads. Beside him, Lara Lor-Van keeps one calm hand against his wrist. Perhaps Jor-El already suspects the Science Council won't evacuate a single district; maybe he speaks only so history, if any history survives, records that someone tried. Deep beneath their boots, radioactive green seams are chewing through Krypton's iron heart like rot in sweet fruit.

Chief Magistrate Ro-Zar cuts the channel mid-sentence.

Silence settles over the laboratory. Outside the high lancet window, Kandor's evening sky bruises an unnatural, surgical violet.

No thunder precedes it. Not even wind. A vertical cylinder of green-and-violet luminescence drops straight from high orbit, neatly stenciling Kandor's twelve-mile perimeter wall as though some vast draftsman in the dark has drawn a circle with a compass. Sky-sleds stall in mid-air. Birds freeze between wingbeats. Before the Science Guard can prime a single thermal lance, every spire, park, bridge, and living soul in Kandor pulls inward toward a blinding focal point, shrinking to the breadth of a fingernail and rising smoothly into the clouds.

Two heartbeats. Kandor is gone. Nothing remains between the coastal cliffs save a smoking, glassy bowl carved clean out of the bedrock.

Nine months later, panic still hasn't reached the marble plazas of Kryptonopolis, hastily anointed planetary capital while bureaucrats blame Kandor's disappearance on a freak magnetic sinkhole. Down in Jor-El's private subterranean vault, miles south of the doomed senate, plaster dust sifts continuously from the ceiling beams. Ground tremors rattle racks of crystal memory cylinders. In a padded cradle at the center of the floor, two-year-old Kal-El laughs at the noise, kicking chubby legs beneath three tightly woven blankets—one scarlet, one deep blue, one bright canary-yellow—and swatting at a holographic mobile of a distant yellow star ringed by nine tiny worlds.

"Earth," Lara whispers, testing the foreign syllable on her tongue. It sounds rough to her, almost primitive, though Jor-El promises its yellow sunlight will drink into their boy's cells like warm milk, making his skin harder than starship hull-plate and his bones virtually unbreakable.

Jor-El says he could have built the silver-finned prototype wide enough for three if the Council hadn't impounded his fuel cells last week. That might even be true, or it might be the merciful fiction a husband offers his wife during the final four minutes of the world. Together they lift Kal-El into the narrow cockpit of the three-meter test rocket, tucking a glowing crystalline chronicle beside his cheek and sealing the transparent canopy just as emerald fire splits the observatory floor from wall to wall.

Lara presses her palm against the glass. Kal-El presses a tiny hand back, dark curl bobbing over his forehead.

Jor-El yanks the manual release. Solid-fuel boosters roar up the mountain shaft, punching through black sulfur clouds into cold starlight at the exact instant Krypton's core yields—not in a slow crumble, as Jor-El's conservative models predicted, but in a single blinding detonation that scatters billions of irradiated green shards into the dark.

text:
As Climax Foods CEO Oliver Zahn serves up a plate of vegan brie, feta, and blue cheese in his offices in Emeryville, California, I’m keeping my expectations modest. Most vegan cheese falls into an edible uncanny valley full of discomforting not-quite-right versions of the real thing. But the brie I taste today is smooth, rich, and velvety—and delicious. I could easily believe it was made from cow’s milk, but it is made entirely from plants. And it couldn’t have come into existence, says Zahn, without the use of machine learning.

Climax Foods is one of several startups, also including Shiru of Alameda, California, and NotCo of Chile, that have used artificial intelligence to design plant-based foods. The companies train algorithms on datasets of ingredients with desirable traits like flavor, scent, or stretchability. Then they use AI to comb troves of data to develop new combinations of those ingredients that perform similarly.

“Traditional ingredient discovery can take years and tens of millions of dollars, and what results are ingredients only incrementally better than the previous generation,” says Shiru CEO Jasmin Hume, who wrote her PhD thesis on protein engineering. “[Now] we can go from scratch, meaning what nature has to offer; pick out the proteins that will function best; and prototype and test them in about three months.”

Not everyone in the industry is bullish about AI-assisted ingredient discovery. Jonathan McIntyre, a food consultant who formerly headed R&D teams in both beverages and snacks at Pepsi, thinks the technology is “significantly” overhyped as a tool for his field. “AI is only as good as the data you feed it,” he says. And given how jealously food companies guard formulas and proprietary information, he adds, there won’t necessarily be sufficient data to yield productive results. McIntyre has a cautionary tale: during his stint at Pepsi, the company attempted to use IBM’s Watson to create a better soda. “It formulated the worst-tasting thing ever,” he says.

Climax Foods circumvented the data scarcity problem by creating its own training sets to essentially reverse-engineer why cheese tastes so good. “When we started, there was very little data on why an animal product tastes the way it does—animal cheddar, blue, brie, mozzarella—because it is what it is,” says Zahn, who previously headed data science for Google’s massive ads business. “There [was] no commercial reason to understand it.”  

In the food science lab on the ground floor of the Climax offices, on the site of an old chocolate factory, Zahn shows off some of the instruments his team used to build its data trove. There’s a machine that uses ion chromatography to show the precise balance of different acids after bacterial strains break down lactose. A mass spectrometer acts like an “electronic nose” to reveal which volatile compounds generate our olfactory response to food. A device called a rheometer tracks how a cheese responds to physical deformation; part of our response to cheese is based on how it reacts to slicing or chewing. The cheese data creates target baselines of performance that an AI can try to reach with different combinations of plant ingredients.

Using educated guesswork about which plants might perform well as substitutes, Climax food scientists have created more than 5,000 cheese prototypes in the past four years. With the same lab instruments employed on animal cheese, the Climax team performs an analysis that includes roughly 50 different assays for texture and flavor, generating millions of data points in the process. The AI is trained on these prototypes, and the algorithm then suggests mixtures that might perform even better. The team tries them out and keeps iterating. “You vary all the input knobs, you measure the outputs, and then you try to squeeze the difference between the output and your animal target to be as small as possible,” Zahn says. Including small-scale “micro-prototypes,” he estimates, Climax has analyzed roughly 100,000 plant ingredient combinations.

Tasting and subtly adjusting the ingredient blends in so many prototypes by hand would take several thousand years, Zahn says. But starting from zero in early 2020, he and his AI-aided team were able to formulate their first cheese and bring it to market in April 2023.  

The plant constituents of that product, a vegan blue cheese, are hardly exotic. The top four ingredients are pumpkin seeds, coconut oil, lima beans, and hemp protein powder. And yet Dominique Crenn, a Michelin-starred chef, described it as “soft, buttery, and surprisingly rich—beyond imagination for a vegan cheese.”  

Bel Group, the maker of Laughing Cow, has an agreement to license the company’s products, and a second large producer that Zahn cannot yet publicly name has also signed on. He is currently beating the venture capital bushes for a funding round and hopes to begin selling the brie and feta later this year. 

Unlike Watson’s ill-fated attempt to formulate a better Pepsi, the Climax algorithms can pull together ingredients in new ways that seem like alchemy. “There is an interaction of one component with another component that triggers a flavor or sensation that you didn’t expect,” Zahn says. “It’s not like just the sum of the two components—it’s something completely different.”  

One reason to develop alternatives to dairy-based cheese is its environmental cost: by weight, cheese has a higher carbon footprint than either chicken or pork, and humans eat roughly 22 million tons of it each year. For Zahn, the answer is not asking consumers to settle for a rubbery, bland substitute—but offering a plant-based version that tastes as good or better and could cost much less to make.

Andrew Rosenblum’s writing has appeared in New Scientist, Popular Science, Wired, and many other places.

50 OLD-SCHOOL REMEDIES & SAFER UPDATES 👇

1️⃣ HONEY FOR COUGHS

May soothe coughing. Never give honey to babies under 12 months.

Comfortably warm water or tea can soothe an irritated throat.

3️⃣ SALTWATER GARGLE

Adults: dissolve ½ teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water. Gargle and spit.

4️⃣ COOL, SOFT FOODS

Soft foods and ice pops can make a sore throat more comfortable.

5️⃣ SALINE NASAL SPRAY

Prepared saline spray or drops can help with stuffy nasal passages.

6️⃣ SAFE NASAL RINSING

Use a proper saline mixture with distilled or sterile water. Follow device instructions.

Certain preparations have traditional use for mild bloating. Clinical evidence is limited; follow labeling.

8️⃣ GINGER

Ginger tea or foods may help nausea. Check pregnancy supplements with a pharmacist.

9️⃣ PEPPERMINT TEA

May help nausea. Skip it if it aggravates your heartburn.

🔟 SMALL, LIGHT MEALS

Smaller portions eaten more frequently may be easier on a queasy stomach.

1️⃣1️⃣ FRESH AIR

A little fresh air may help ease nausea.

1️⃣2️⃣ CARAWAY TEA

A traditional option for mild gas and bloating; reliable clinical evidence remains limited.

1️⃣3️⃣ PRUNES

Prunes or prune juice can help with constipation.

1️⃣4️⃣ RAISINS AND APRICOTS

These fruits supply fiber and sorbitol, which can help soften stools.

1️⃣5️⃣ OATS AND BRAN

Gradually adding these fiber sources may improve bowel regularity.

1️⃣6️⃣ WATER WITH FIBER

Drink sufficient fluids as you increase fiber. Follow any prescribed fluid restrictions.

1️⃣7️⃣ A DAILY WALK

Regular movement can help relieve constipation.

1️⃣8️⃣ A TOILET FOOTSTOOL

Supporting your feet with your knees above your hips may make passing stool easier.

For reflux, finish eating three to four hours before bed.

2️⃣0️⃣ A LOOSER WAISTBAND

Avoid tight clothing around your stomach when heartburn troubles you.

2️⃣1️⃣ SLOW BREATHING

Slow, comfortable breathing can help you relax when pain makes you tense.

2️⃣2️⃣ QUIET REST

Resting in a quiet, dark room may help during a familiar migraine.

2️⃣3️⃣ REGULAR MEALS

Skipping meals can trigger headaches. Keep a regular eating schedule.

2️⃣4️⃣ A COOL FOREHEAD CLOTH

A cool cloth on your head may ease migraine discomfort.

2️⃣5️⃣ A WARM NECK PACK

A comfortably warm, wrapped pack may ease ordinary neck pain. Protect your skin.

2️⃣6️⃣ GENTLE MOVEMENT

Once pain allows, gently move a recovering sprain to help prevent stiffness.

2️⃣7️⃣ A WRAPPED COLD PACK

For a fresh sprain, apply through a cloth for up to 20 minutes.

2️⃣8️⃣ ELEVATION

Support a sprained limb on pillows to help reduce swelling.

2️⃣9️⃣ REST FROM PAINFUL ACTIVITIES

Protect a fresh strain and pause activities that make it hurt.

3️⃣0️⃣ A WARM BATH

Warm water may ease muscle spasm. Avoid heat on fresh, swollen injuries.

3️⃣1️⃣ RUNNING WATER FOR BURNS

Cool a fresh thermal burn under cool running water for 20 minutes. Skip butter, oils, and raw egg.

3️⃣2️⃣ A COOL SUNBURN COMPRESS

Gently apply a cool, damp cloth to sunburned skin.

3️⃣3️⃣ ALOE MOISTURIZER

An aloe-containing moisturizer may soothe mild sunburn on intact skin.

3️⃣4️⃣ COLLOIDAL OATMEAL

A colloidal oatmeal bath can soothe itchy, sunburned skin.

3️⃣5️⃣ CALAMINE LOTION

Use as labeled for itching and sunburn discomfort.

3️⃣6️⃣ DIRECT PRESSURE

Press firmly on a bleeding cut with clean gauze. Uncontrolled bleeding needs emergency help.

3️⃣7️⃣ CLEAN-WATER WOUND RINSING

Rinse minor cuts with clean running water. Keep kitchen ingredients out of wounds.

3️⃣8️⃣ PLAIN PETROLEUM JELLY

A thin layer on a clean minor cut helps keep it moist.

3️⃣9️⃣ A CLEAN COVERING

Cover minor cuts and change the dressing when wet or dirty.

4️⃣0️⃣ A COLD CLOTH FOR BITES

A clean, cold cloth can help reduce swelling from an ordinary insect bite.

4️⃣1️⃣ A WARM COMPRESS FOR BOILS

Hold a clean, warm cloth against a small boil. Don’t squeeze it; fever or facial boils need medical advice.

4️⃣2️⃣ FREQUENT DRINKS DURING FEVER

Drink enough to avoid dehydration, following any prescribed fluid restrictions.

4️⃣3️⃣ REST DURING FEVER

Give yourself time to recover. A worsening or persistent fever needs medical advice.

4️⃣4️⃣ A REGULAR WAKE-UP TIME

Getting up at the same time daily supports a steadier sleep routine.

4️⃣5️⃣ A DARK, QUIET BEDROOM

Reduce light and noise when sleep is difficult.

4️⃣6️⃣ LEMON BALM

Traditionally used for mild stress and sleep complaints. Clinical evidence remains limited.

4️⃣7️⃣ CHAMOMILE TEA

A caffeine-free evening option. Related plant allergies can increase reaction risk; medication interactions are possible.

4️⃣8️⃣ A SALTWATER DENTAL RINSE

Adults can gently rinse and spit for temporary comfort while arranging dental care.

4️⃣9️⃣ SOFT FOODS FOR TOOTH PAIN

Choose soft foods and avoid chewing on the painful tooth.

5️⃣0️⃣ LABELED CLOVE-OIL DENTAL PRODUCTS

For adults, these may offer temporary toothache relief. Follow instructions, avoid gum contact, and see a dentist.

Purification & Doorway Marking: Wake up early, take a bath, and wear clean clothes. Clean your home altar, shop, or office, and draw a Swastika with "Shubh" and "Labh" using red kumkum on both sides of the main entrance.
Altar Setup: Spread a clean red or yellow cloth on a wooden platform (chowki). Place idols or pictures of Lord Ganesh, Goddess Lakshmi, and Goddess Saraswati. Keep your new account ledgers (chopda), pens, cash box, or work laptops beside them.
Invocation & Lamp Lighting: Light a pure ghee lamp (diya) and incense sticks. Offer water to the Sun God (Surya Arghya) and sprinkle Gangajal around the puja space.
Worshipping the Deities: Begin by offering vermilion (kumkum), sandalwood paste (chandan), unbroken rice (akshat), flowers, and durva grass to Lord Ganesh. Next, offer red flowers, lotus seeds, sweets, and fruits to Goddess Lakshmi and Goddess Saraswati.
Chopda Pujan (Opening Account Books): Open the first page of your new ledger. Draw a kumkum Swastika in the center, write "Shree Ganeshay Namah" at the top, and write "Shubh" on the left and "Labh" on the right. Make an auspicious first financial entry or note a prayer for honest earnings.
Mantra Chanting & Aarti: Chant the Sri Ganesh and Sri Lakshmi mantras, perform the final Aarti, and distribute sweets (prasad) to family members, staff, and your first customers of the day.

text:
Japan’s Forgotten Harvest Festival — What Was Lost After World War II? 🌾

Every November 23, Japan celebrates Labor Thanksgiving Day.

But long before this modern holiday existed, the date held a very different meaning.

It was Niinamesai, one of Japan’s most important traditional ceremonies.

And its story reveals how deeply a nation’s culture can change after defeat in war.

For centuries, rice has been more than food in Japan.

It has shaped agriculture, communities, religious beliefs, and the Japanese relationship with nature.

During Niinamesai, the Emperor offers newly harvested rice and other produce to the deities, gives thanks for the harvest, and partakes of the sacred food himself.

The ceremony expresses a profound idea.

Human life depends on blessings beyond human effort alone.

The earth, rain, sunlight, changing seasons, and countless hands make every harvest possible.

Before World War II, November 23 was a national holiday dedicated to this ancient ceremony.

Then Japan lost the war.

Under the Allied occupation, Japan’s political institutions and relationship between religion and the state underwent sweeping reforms.

In 1948, Niinamesai was replaced on the national holiday calendar by Labor Thanksgiving Day.

The date remained unchanged.

But its official meaning shifted from an imperial harvest ritual to honoring labor, production, and mutual gratitude.

Japanese lawmakers helped shape the new holiday, so the change cannot be attributed solely to GHQ.

Yet the cultural consequences remain significant.

When a traditional religious observance disappears from a nation’s public calendar, something more than its name can be lost.

People may still enjoy the holiday.

But the beliefs and memories that gave it meaning can gradually fade.

For those who value Japan’s spiritual heritage, this represents a profound loss.

And yet, Niinamesai never disappeared.

Every November 23, the Emperor continues to perform the ceremony at the Imperial Palace.

The Imperial Household Agency describes it as the most important of the regularly held imperial ceremonies.

Shrines throughout Japan also continue to give thanks for the harvest.

The tradition survived, even as its place in the national holiday calendar changed.

History shows that military defeat can transform far more than governments and borders.

It can reshape how a people understand their own past.

But a modern society should be able to uphold religious freedom and the separation of religion and state without forgetting its ancestral traditions.

Respecting cultural heritage does not mean everyone must share the same beliefs.

It means recognizing the traditions that have shaped generations of human lives.

A truly mature international society must respect the cultural and spiritual heritage of every people, including those defeated in war.

On November 23, Japan gives thanks for work.

But behind that modern holiday remains an older expression of gratitude.

Its name is Niinamesai.

And its story deserves to be remembered.

text:
Sophie Rain came home from the Super Bowl and found a stranger walking down her stairs - shirtless, with his belongings already moved in. He'd smashed every window, barricaded himself inside, and told police they were married. He said his last name was "Rain." That they'd taken a blood oath. SWAT, the FBI, and the Coast Guard surrounded the house. A judge later ruled him legally insane. She's 20 years old, a devout Christian, claims to be a virgin, and has made over $100 million selling solo photos of herself on the internet.

Sophie Rain grew up in Tampa, Florida, going to church every Sunday with her devoutly Christian parents. Nothing about her childhood suggested what was coming. She was working as a waitress in 2023 when her older sister Sierra posted photos of herself in Spider-Man costumes on OnlyFans. A viral NSFW clip started circulating — and the internet was convinced it was Sophie. It wasn't. She denied it over and over again, but nobody believed her. So she made a decision that would change everything: she ran with it. She created an OnlyFans account, leaned into the Spider-Man persona, and within weeks had millions of followers pouring in across every platform. Her boss at the restaurant found out and fired her on the spot. She didn't need the job anymore. In her first year on OnlyFans - November 2023 to November 2024 - Sophie Rain earned $43 million. More than Lionel Messi's base salary at Inter Miami. More than most Fortune 500 CEOs. And she did it posting solo content only, with no collaborations, no partners, and no explicit scenes with anyone. Her secret, she says, is the paradox itself: "Why I think I'm so popular? Because I've never had sex before. I'm still a virgin." A Christian virgin who makes millions selling photos of her body. The internet couldn't look away.

By 2025, her earnings had hit $83 million in a single year. She paid $30.7 million in federal taxes alone - a 37% top bracket. Her top subscriber, a man known only as "Charley," had spent over $1.4 million on her content, with reports suggesting he tipped nearly $5 million total. CamSoda offered her $250,000 to lose her virginity on a livestream. She refused. Companies kept throwing money at her to break the brand. She kept saying no. In December 2024, she co-founded the Bop House - a waterfront Miami mansion where eight female OnlyFans creators aged 18 to 22 lived together, collaborating on content. Between them they had over 33 million followers. It was supposed to be the ultimate content empire. Then came the Super Bowl weekend in February 2025. Sophie and the girls left for the game. While they were gone, a man named Connor Litka from Texas tracked them to their Fort Lauderdale rental. He smashed the windows, disabled the alarm, and moved himself in. When Sophie came home and opened the front door, she saw him coming down the stairs without a shirt - like he owned the place. The girls fled. Police arrived. Then SWAT. Then the FBI. Because the house sat on a canal, the Coast Guard was called in too. Litka barricaded himself inside and told officers he was the new owner of the home, that his last name was "Rain," that he and Sophie were married, and that they had taken a blood oath together. Sophie spent a full week speaking with FBI detectives afterward. Litka was eventually arrested and ruled legally insane by a judge. He had been tracking her online, convinced they were in a relationship that never existed. Sophie later stepped away from the Bop House entirely, saying she wanted a quieter life. By January 2026, she posted a screen recording of her OnlyFans dashboard showing $101 million in lifetime gross earnings. She earns more per year than LeBron James. She has 9 million followers on TikTok, 5 million on Instagram, and 3 million on Snapchat. She still calls herself a virgin. She still goes to church. And she still sleeps with one eye open.

Is it possible to sell your body without ever being touched - and still lose everything that made you feel safe?

A Delhi Police chargesheet alleges that an Indian Air Force Wing Commander shared classified military information with a suspected Pakistani intelligence operative over WhatsApp.

The officer allegedly shared a page of a secret war plan after receiving an explicit photograph, and reportedly offered to share more pages in exchange for additional photographs.

The leaked information allegedly included details of a secret drone unit, its capabilities, fighter aircraft deployments in Leh and a military exercise in Suratgarh.

Police also allege that he facilitated the installation of spyware on devices belonging to five subordinates.

The officer faces charges under the Official Secrets Act. The allegations are yet to be proven in court.

#MahaPeriyava 
Compiled by Jagadguru Sri Maha Periyava - Kanchi Paramacharya/Fb

It was a Sunday evening in summer. Sri Maha Periyava was giving darshan sitting inside His mena (palanquin). Devotees in large numbers had turned up for darshan. Offers of plates after plates of fruits, raisins, sugar lumps and honey bottles were on the ground outside the palanquin.

Suddenly an army of monkeys landed there. In the bustle that followed, they mauled and ate the fruits; rolled the honey bottles on the floor.

The disciples were worried that they might go to Periyava and try to do some mischief.

Not a sign of distress was seen on Periyava's face. An ishvaragya (divine order) of not to harm them came from Him in the gesture of a snap of fingers! The loving devotees who came with staffs, stopped in their tracks, remaining motionless like the staffs they carried.

At length, finishing their work, the monkeys went away for their Rama Karyam. Periyava told a story to the devotees.

A village in Thanjavur district could not withstand the trouble given by monkeys. A man hit a monkey that got caught unexpectedly, with a stick. Owing to internal injuries the monkey died after a few days.

The girl child that was born next to him was speech impaired. The time to get that girl married came up.

The couple came to Periyava, narrated their sin and wept.

"Make a monkey figure out of clay and give it as an offering to the temple of your village deity. Give the girl in marriage to one who gives his heartfelt consent to marry her."

It happened in the same way. Later it was learnt that the girl who was married gave birth to a child who spoke intelligently.

"You should never beat the monkeys. You should show compassion to them. They come in the parampara (ancestry) of Ram Sevaks. Even though they might give us trouble, we must leave them, thinking of Anjaneya."

The loving devotees went melting, hearing the story and teaching from Periyava Himself.

Sarvam Sri Krishnarpanam 🙏🏻

text:
THEOLOGICAL MUSINGS: MINI REALMS OF GRACE AS A WITNESS

Sometimes the inbreaking of the realm of God occurs in history and in our time—touching individuals and communities—and creates mini realms of grace and agape love in the world. As a witness to a better way of life, they bring healing, peace, and reconciliation to a broken world, all grounded in zoe, the resurrectional life and power of Christ. For example, Clarence Jordan and Koinonia Farm remain deeply relevant today as a model for racial reconciliation, economic justice, sustainable agriculture, and radical Christian community living. AJ

THE CHRISTIAN WITNESS OF THE KOINONIA FARM

Radical Racial Solidarity and Inclusion: Founded in 1942 in Sumter County, Georgia, Koinonia Farm was built as an intentional, interracial Christian community during the height of Jim Crow segregation. In an era of lingering social division, their model of Black and white people living, eating, and laboring together as equals offers an enduring challenge to racial prejudice.

Economic Justice and Resistance to Racial Capitalism: Jordan rejected both systemic wealth disparities and the complicity of mainstream religious institutions in supporting economic oppression. The community pooled land, money, and labor, proving that faith requires tangible economic sharing rather than just abstract spiritual belief.

The Roots of Habitat for Humanity: Out of Koinonia Farm grew the Fund For Humanity, developed by Jordan and Millard and Linda Fuller, which pioneered zero-interest, partnership housing for low-income families. This direct-action approach evolved straight into Habitat for Humanity, which has built homes globally.

Nonviolent Witness Against Violence and War: Facing Ku Klux Klan bombings, gunfire, and total economic boycotts, Jordan and his community refused to retaliate with violence, leaning instead on active peacemaking and love for their enemies.

Contextualizing Faith (The Cotton Patch Gospels): Jordan translated the New Testament into contemporary Southern vernacular (writing the Cotton Patch versions), famously reframing ancient biblical narratives—such as equating the crucifixion with modern racial lynchings—to strip away religious hypocrisy and force people to confront the real-world demands of the Gospel.

Sustainable Agriculture and Land Stewardship: The community viewed healing depleted soil and working the land cooperatively as an integral part of restoring human dignity and local economies.

Sources: The Radical Southern Farmer White Christians Should Know About by Mitchell Atencio/SOJOURNERS, Koinonia Farm (1942- ) BLACK PAST, Clarence Jordan and the Presence of the Gospel The Koinonia Farm as Contemporary Theo Ethical Protest/ACADEMIA, Clarence Jordan and Habitat for Humanity/HABITAT FOR HUMANITY, The Inconvenient Gospel: A Southern Prophet Tackles War, Wealth, Race, and Religion/PLOUGH PUBLISHING, Koinonia Farm, & Google

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

Clarence Jordan was a farmer and Greek New Testament scholar from rural Georgia who dedicated his life and ministry to advocating for those living in poverty and for the equality of all people.

He also is considered the spiritual father of Habitat for Humanity, and our operational headquarters in Americus, Georgia, now bears his name.

In 1942, Jordan founded Koinonia Farm, an interracial Christian farming community near Americus where members worked together for the common good and all persons were treated equally. Today, Koinonia continues as a working farm and Christian community.

“Clarence said, ‘Before we can do anything, we have to be something. Our actions have to spring from our inner character,’” says Bren Dubay, executive director of Koinonia Farm. “We really need to take this quote from Clarence to heart. We want ‘doing’ to come out of who we are.” via HABITAT FOR HUMANITY

THE GOOD NEWS OF THE RESURRECTION OF JESUS
"The resurrection of Jesus was simply God's unwillingness to take our 'no' for an answer. He raised Jesus, not as an invitation to us to come to heaven when we die, but as a declaration that he himself has now established permanent, eternal residence here on earth. He is standing beside us, strengthening us in this life. The good news of the resurrection of Jesus is not that we shall die and go home to be with him, but that he has risen and comes home with us, bringing all his hungry, naked, thirsty, sick prisoner brothers with him." Another caption scored as closed. Another package. Another open file.

Ottawa and Ontario have “put an aggressive package to Stellantis to prevent the sale.” The arithmetic has not moved. The Brampton Assembly Plant has sat idle since late 2023. Roughly 2,200 workers remain on layoff after three years of paid idleness. Under the 2022 Strategic Innovation Fund agreement, Ottawa committed up to $529 million for retooling Brampton and Windsor so the sites would produce electrified vehicles, including the Jeep Compass. At least $220 million was already disbursed. Stellantis then paused the retooling, shifted the Compass mandate to Illinois after U.S. tariffs, and signed an asset-purchase agreement to sell the plant to Roshel. Primary reporting shows federal officials were briefed on the Roshel discussions for months. The company has offered to repay $24 million. The minister now speaks of hundreds of millions and a 30-day clock while floating new scenarios to the global CEO.

A new subsidy package does not restore vehicle production, full-time employment at the prior baseline, or productivity per worker. Rooms are not steel. An “aggressive package” is process language. It names no measurable outcome a citizen can score against primary sources, no fixed scoring date, no owner by office who answers when the arithmetic fails, and no result that would prove the claim wrong. Selling the plant to a defence contractor may return some activity to the site. It does not close the auto-assembly file that was funded on the premise of sustained vehicle production. Canadian labour productivity remains roughly 26 per cent below the American path since the late 1990s. Business investment per worker sits in the mid-50-cent range on the U.S. dollar. Another cheque does not finish those rows.

Name the test that would close this caption. One published, dated primary-source result showing measurable full-time employment at or above the prior baseline of approximately 2,200 jobs at the Brampton site under a single readable commercial arrangement a banker, a union member, and a citizen can check the same way; sustained production of vehicles, or an equivalent finished industrial output that survives the next tariff cycle; a fixed scoring date of 30 June 2027; a named owner by office; and a result that would prove the claim wrong: residual layoffs, continued process language, clawback of only a fraction of the advanced funds without restored capacity, or the site permanently converted out of auto assembly. On that date, the entry is scored PASS or FAILED against primary sources. The original wording is never edited. Failures name the blocking layer. A ministerial caption is not that record. An idle plant funded for electrified Jeeps and then sold for armoured vehicles is not capacity online.

Production before process.  
Capacity before the next ministerial package.  
Evidence before narrative.  
Citizens first.  
Canada first.  
One law for all.

Truth Marker: π ≈ 3.14159  
Barry E. Sharp 🇨🇦

@GovWesMoore must cut spending to reduce the budget and make Maryland affordable. It was never about Trump.  

🚨Will he choose reduced spending like a leader or raise taxes again like a politician?🚨

To close our $2.57B–$3.1B structural deficit without tax hikes, combine major formula adjustments, strict audits, perk elimination, and debt collection.

1. Major Policy changes and program changes 
• Delay or scale back the Blueprint education mandate ($500M–$1.5B+ annually). Freezing phase-in of new mandates under the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future—projected to need $1.57B General Fund support in FY 2028—offers the largest savings.
• Enact 10% across-the-board agency and university cuts ($300M–$600M annually). Apply the maximum 10% reductions modeled by agencies and public universities in September 2026 via hiring freezes, vacancy elimination, and lower overhead.
• Contain Medicaid and disability services growth ($200M–$500M annually). Cap provider rate increases and tighten eligibility for programs like the Developmental Disabilities Administration to slow growth, though federal matching funds decrease.
• Slash nonprofit grants and discretionary earmarks ($100M–$800M+ pool). Audit, cap, or eliminate parts of the $800M+ in nonprofit grants and legislative bond initiatives for local projects.
• Eliminate state-funded programs for undocumented immigrants ($67M–$100M+ annually). End the Healthy Babies Equity Act prenatal program (~$58M+) and in-state college tuition/financial aid subsidies (~$9M). Federal law blocks cuts to K–12 or emergency care.

2. Debt Collection, Audit Recoveries & Contract Waste (Tens to Hundreds of Millions)
• Collect unpursued delinquent taxes and state debts ($600M+ taxes / $240.8M Central Collection). Enforce tools from 2026 audits of the Comptroller’s Office ($600M+ uncollected taxes) and Department of Budget and Management’s Central Collection Unit ($240.8M unpursued non-tax debts).
• Recover improper healthcare and benefit payments ($51M+ identified). Collect $41.9M from provider errors and fraud (Office of the Inspector General for Health) plus $9.2M in improper Medicaid payments for deceased or incarcerated individuals.
• Cut SNAP payment errors to avoid federal fines ($28M+ in past penalties). Reduce Maryland’s 13.08% food stamp error rate below 6% to stop penalties and improper payments.
• Curb untracked outside legal fees and failed IT contracts ($96M+ combined). Halt $62.6M in untracked private law firm contracts across 53 agencies and use milestone payments to avoid failures like the $32.5M eMaryland Marketplace Advantage platform.

3. Legislative Perks, Travel & Discretionary Expenses (Hundreds of Thousands to Millions)
• Require receipts for lawmaker meal allowances. Legislators get a $63 daily meal allowance during session without receipts, unlike regular employees.
• Eliminate district expense stipends and automatic pay hikes. Cut automatic salary increases (from $52,000 in 2023 to $56,600 in 2026 for legislators; $73,600 for presiding officers) and annual allowances for in-district travel ($750), phones ($2,000), postage ($1,000), newspapers ($750), and smartphone data ($50/month). (Reversing Baltimore County’s 74% pay raise saves ~$458,750/year, separate from the state budget.)
• Enforce bans on luxury state travel and unmonitored trips. A September 2026 audit found prohibited business- and first-class domestic flights and poor monitoring of international travel. Require economy-only travel and pre-approval for out-of-state conferences.
• Ban campaign funds for personal lifestyle and party expenses. Lawmakers have used political accounts for luxury resorts, leisure travel, and dining. Tighten election laws to prohibit personal use.
• Require elected officials to pay personal legal defense costs. Prohibit the Board of Public Works from using taxpayer funds (e.g., $50,000 in October 2026 for Gov. Wes Moore’s defamation defense).

text:
As mentioned earlier, it’s been a mixed bag for Kyle Whittingham’s legacy in Utah. Not all bad, and not all good.

His standing is mainly tarnished because a segment of people inside the program and among the fan base felt the departure was a betrayal. Others remain on good terms with him.

For roughly five years, Whittingham had floated the idea of retirement. It was never official, but the widespread expectation was that 2025 would be his final season. He had told both media and athletic director Mark Harlan that he preferred not to coach past 2025 so he could spend more time with his grandchildren.

In December 2025 he had a change of heart and wanted to stay a few more years. He requested a significant raise and additional resources. Utah countered with terms that would have required him to cede substantial control to his successor, Morgan Scalley, who was already designated as head coach in waiting. The sides could not reach an agreement. Harlan effectively pushed Whittingham toward an exit while allowing him a paid transition role.

Whittingham officially stepped down and was initially celebrated. Fans cheered him at Utah Jazz games and around Salt Lake City.
Roughly two weeks later, after the sudden coaching vacancy in Ann Arbor, Michigan offered him the job. He accepted.

The move itself was not the most dramatic coaching departure in recent memory, but what stung many Utah fans and people inside the program was that Whittingham took multiple coaches and players with him. 

Some, including Scalley, still value the relationship. Others, notably Harlan, do not.

The financial side added to the friction. As part of the separation agreement, Utah is paying Whittingham a $13.5 million transition bonus. His brother, Freddie Whittingham, also joined the Michigan staff. Utah has sued Freddie for breach of contract, alleging he left without proper notice, failed to honor his buyout, and recruited players while still under contract with the Utes.

Some people in Utah remain friendly with Whittingham, but the manner of the departure created enough residual damage that the university is unlikely to formally honor him in the near term. That could change in five to ten years. For now, a meaningful number of people in the program feel betrayed.

He could have remained a universally beloved figure in Utah forever. He chose a different path. That is his right, but Utah football does not owe him anything further. 

The two sides went their separate ways.

text:
SIGNAL INTELLIGENCE BRIEF
Published: November 13, 2026 | 3:46 PM ET

Thesis:
The selling is concentrated in big technology stocks while credit, bonds and the average stock hold up, so this is a rotation that has not yet become a broad retreat.

WHAT MATTERS
Leader: Health Care +6.74% | Laggard: Information Technology -8.03%
The S&P 500 is down **1.67% over four weeks**, but that headline hides a split. The Nasdaq 100 is down 4.87%, while the equal-weight S&P 500, where every company counts the same, is up **3.16%** and the Russell 2000 of smaller companies is up 2.32%. The S&P 500 itself is cap-weighted, meaning the biggest companies count the most, so a few falling giants pull it 4.83 percentage points below the average stock. Consumer discretionary (+6.56%) and financials (+5.59%) also lead.

HY OAS 320bps (-11bps 4wk) | 12m avg 290bps
This is the credit spread, the extra yield risky companies pay over the government. Spreads are 11bps tighter over four weeks, which says lenders are not worried yet.

0/6 basket assets down >1% today (cross-asset drawdown)
None of the six major asset baskets we track fell more than 1% today, so the broad market is calmer than the technology sell-off suggests.

WHAT IS HIDDEN
Start with what long-term borrowing costs are made of. The 10-year Treasury yield, about 5.15%, has three parts: the real yield after inflation (2.78%, down 6bps over four weeks), the inflation rate the bond market expects, called breakeven (2.24%, down 8bps), and the term premium, the extra yield investors demand for locking money up for ten years instead of rolling short-term bills.

Kim-Wright 0.87% (-20bps 4wk) | ACM (NY Fed) 0.68% (-7bps 4wk)
These are two models of the term premium, with readings as of November 6 and no new release since. Both fell over four weeks. With all three parts of the yield easing, long yields are not being pushed up by inflation worry or by a demand for extra pay, and the high yield reflects a high real return on offer.

Bond volatility says the same thing quietly. The MOVE index measures how much traders expect Treasury yields to swing, the way VIX does for stocks. MOVE is **98.80**, down 2.29 points over four weeks and just under 100, against a VIX of 19.20, so bonds are still expected to swing about five times as much as stocks. VVIX, which prices insurance against jumps in VIX itself, is 101.3, a sign that some investors are paying for protection while the main gauge looks calm.

TGA $912.1bn (-8.1bn 4wk) | RRP $0.3bn
Liquidity gives a small cushion. The TGA is the Treasury's cash balance, and it stood at $912.1bn on November 10, so the government is not draining cash from the banking system. The overnight funding rate SOFR is 3.9%, though the Fed's reverse repo facility (RRP), where money funds park spare cash, holds just $0.3bn, so that buffer is nearly gone.

Treasuries held at the Fed for foreign central banks and official accounts: $2,531.4bn | -$19.1bn on the week | -$17.8bn over 4 weeks
This is the November 11 reading, and it is also down $217.7bn over a year, a slow leak in one source of bond demand. There has been no new 10-year or 30-year auction since October 8, and as of November 4 primary dealers, the banks that must bid at auctions, held a net $467.3bn of Treasuries financed with $3166.1bn of repo borrowing.

The last hidden piece is leverage. Leveraged exchange-traded funds borrow to multiply daily moves, and trading in the leveraged semiconductor fund SOXL equals 79.29% of the volume of the chip stocks it tracks, with margin debt (money borrowed against stock portfolios) also at a high level. That leverage sits in technology, the sector down 8.03%.

WHAT IS MISPRICED
Gold is the asset not doing its job. It is down 7.14% over four weeks and 17.09% over twelve, even though real yields eased 6bps and Iran headlines continue on November 13. Gold normally gains when real yields fall or when fear rises, and neither held. Credit may also be priced too easily: spreads at 320bps have tightened, yet they remain above their 12-month average of 290bps while the biggest stocks are being sold.

WHAT MARKETS DISAGREE ON
Bonds and commodities point to a growth scare. Breakevens, real yields and the term premium all eased, crude is down more than 10% over four weeks and copper is down 7.46%, which together suggest softer demand. Credit and gold disagree: tighter spreads say lenders are relaxed, and falling gold says nobody is rushing to safety. Stocks add a third voice, with defensive sectors up 5.5% against 0.3% for cyclical ones. Our evidence favours the growth-scare reading over an inflation scare, though neither fits cleanly. Households and markets also disagree. The University of Michigan survey puts year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.3% for November, while the bond market's breakeven is 2.24%, though the two cover different horizons.

WHAT TO WATCH NEXT
The stress signal is bond volatility moving back above 100 while credit spreads widen from 320bps, with 50bps of widening in four weeks being the warning line. A VIX above 25 would show stock fear spreading beyond technology. The relief signal is technology and communication services recovering toward the equal-weight index while equity fund flows turn positive. The live event risk is Iran: reporting dated November 13 says US forces shot down two Revolutionary Guards drones over Bahrain and that Israel is preparing scenarios for a renewed war, and crude jumping back would be the first place it shows.
