text:
This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here.

In the world of AI, a lot can happen in a year. Last year, at the beginning of Big Tech’s AI wars, Google announced during its annual I/O conference that it was throwing generative AI at everything, integrating it into its suite of products from Docs to email to e-commerce listings and its chatbot Bard. It was an effort to catch up with competitors like Microsoft and OpenAI, which had unveiled snazzy products like coding assistants and ChatGPT, the product that has done more than any other to ignite the current excitement about AI.

Since then, its ChatGPT competitor chatbot Bard (which, you may recall, temporarily wiped $100 billion off Google’s share price when it made a factual error during the demo) has been replaced by the more advanced Gemini. But, for me, the AI revolution hasn’t felt like one. Instead, it’s been a slow slide toward marginal efficiency gains. I see more autocomplete functions in my email and word processing applications, and Google Docs now offers more ready-made templates. They are not groundbreaking features, but they are also reassuringly inoffensive. 

Google is holding its I/O conference tomorrow, May 14, and we expect them to announce a whole new slew of AI features, further embedding it into everything it does. The company is tight-lipped about its announcements, but we can make educated guesses. There has been a lot of speculation that it will upgrade its crown jewel, Search, with generative AI features that could, for example, go behind a paywall. Perhaps we will see Google’s version of AI agents, a buzzy word that basically means more capable and useful smart assistants able to do more complex tasks, such as booking flights and hotels much as a travel agent would. 

Google, despite having 90% of the online search market, is in a defensive position this year. Upstarts such as Perplexity AI have launched their own versions of AI-powered search to rave reviews, Microsoft’s AI-powered Bing has managed to increase its market share slightly, and OpenAI is working on its own AI-powered online search function and is also reportedly in conversation with Apple to integrate ChatGPT into smartphones. 

There are some hints about what any new AI-powered search features might look like. Felix Simon, a research fellow at the Reuters Institute for Journalism, has been part of the Google Search Generative Experience trial, which is the company’s way of testing new products on a small selection of real users. 

Last month, Simon noticed that his Google searches with links and short snippets from online sources had been replaced by more detailed, neatly packaged AI-generated summaries. He was able to get these results from queries related to nature and health, such as “Do snakes have ears?” Most of the information offered to him was correct, which was a surprise, as AI language models have a tendency to “hallucinate” (which means make stuff up), and they have been criticized for being an unreliable source of information. 

To Simon’s surprise, he enjoyed the new feature. “It’s convenient to ask [the AI] to get something presented just for you,” he says. 

Simon then started using the new AI-powered Google function to search for news items rather than scientific information.

For most of these queries, such as what happened in the UK or Ukraine yesterday, he was simply offered links to news sources such as the BBC and Al Jazeera. But he did manage to get the search engine to generate an overview of recent news items from Germany, in the form of a bullet-pointed list of news headlines from the day before. The first entry was about an attack on Franziska Giffey, a Berlin politician who was assaulted in a library. The AI summary had the date of the attack wrong. But it was so close to the truth that Simon didn’t think twice about its accuracy. 

A quick online search during our call revealed that the rest of the AI-generated news summaries were also littered with inaccuracies. Details were wrong, or the events referred to happened years ago. All the stories were also about terrorism, hate crimes, or violence, with one soccer result thrown in. Omitting headlines on politics, culture, and the economy seems like a weird choice.  

People have a tendency to believe computers to be correct even when they are not, and Simon’s experience is an example of the kinds of problems that might arise when AI models hallucinate. The ease of getting results means that people might unknowingly ingest fake news or wrong information. It’s very problematic if even people like Simon, who are trained to fact-check things and know how AI models work, don’t do their due diligence and assume information is correct. 

Whatever Google announces at I/O tomorrow, there is immense pressure for it to be something that would justify its massive investment into AI. And after a year of experimenting, there also need to be serious improvements in making its generative AI tools more accurate and reliable. 

There are some people in the computer science community who say that hallucinations are an intrinsic part of generative AI that can’t ever be fixed, and that we can never fully trust these systems. But hallucinations will make AI-powered products less appealing to users. And it’s highly unlikely that Google will announce it has fixed this problem at I/O tomorrow. 

If you want to learn more about how Google plans to develop and deploy AI, come and hear from its vice president of AI, Jay Yagnik, at our flagship AI conference, EmTech Digital. It’ll be held at the MIT campus and streamed live online next week on May 22-23.  I’ll be there, along with AI leaders from companies like OpenAI, AWS, and Nvidia, talking about where AI is going next. Nick Clegg, Meta’s president of global affairs, will also join MIT Technology Review’s executive editor Amy Nordrum for an exclusive interview on stage. See you there!

Deeper Learning

Deepfakes of your dead loved ones are a booming Chinese business

Once a week, Sun Kai has a video call with his mother. He opens up about work, the pressures he faces as a middle-aged man, and thoughts that he doesn’t even discuss with his wife. His mother will occasionally make a comment, but mostly, she just listens. That’s because Sun’s mother died five years ago. And the person he’s talking to isn’t actually a person, but a digital replica he made of her—a moving image that can conduct basic conversations. 

AI resurrection: There are plenty of people like Sun who want to use AI to interact with lost loved ones. The market is particularly strong in China, where at least half a dozen companies are now offering such technologies. In some ways, the avatars are the latest manifestation of a cultural tradition: Chinese people have always taken solace from confiding in the dead. Read more from Zeyi Yang. 

Bits and Bytes

Google DeepMind’s new AlphaFold can model a much larger slice of biological life
Google DeepMind has released an improved version of its biology prediction tool, AlphaFold, that can predict the structures not only of proteins but of nearly all the elements of biological life. It’s an exciting development that could help accelerate drug discovery and other scientific research. ​​(MIT Technology Review) 

The way whales communicate is closer to human language than we realized
Researchers used statistical models to analyze whale “codas” and managed to identify a structure to their language that’s similar to features of the complex vocalizations humans use. It’s a small step forward, but it could help unlock a greater understanding of how whales communicate. (MIT Technology Review)

Tech workers should shine a light on the industry’s secretive work with the military
Despite what happens in Google’s executive suites, workers themselves can force change. William Fitzgerald, who leaked information about Google’s controversial Project Maven, has shared how he thinks they can do this. (MIT Technology Review) 

AI systems are getting better at tricking us
A wave of AI systems have “deceived” humans in ways they haven’t been explicitly trained to do, by offering up false explanations for their behavior or concealing the truth from human users and misleading them to achieve a strategic end. This issue highlights how difficult artificial intelligence is to control and the unpredictable ways in which these systems work. (MIT Technology Review) 

Why America needs an Apollo program for the age of AI
AI is crucial to the future security and prosperity of the US. We need to lay the groundwork now by investing in computational power, argues Eric Schmidt. (MIT Technology Review) 

Fooled by AI? These firms sell deepfake detection that’s “REAL 100%”
The AI detection business is booming. There is one catch, however. Detecting AI-generated content is notoriously unreliable, and the tech is still in its infancy. That hasn’t stopped some startup founders (many of whom have no experience or background in AI) from trying to sell services they claim can do so. (The Washington Post) 

The tech-bro turf war over AI’s most hardcore hacker house
A hilarious piece taking an anthropological look at the power struggle between two competing hacker houses in Silicon Valley. The fight is over which house can call itself “AGI House.” (Forbes)

The Pink Suit

On November 22, 1963, in Dallas, Jacqueline Kennedy sat in the back of an open car beside her husband when the shots were fired. 

Minutes later she was at Parkland Hospital still wearing the pink Chanel suit now marked with blood.

Someone offered her clean clothes. She refused. She stayed in the same suit when she boarded Air Force One, when she stood beside Lyndon B. Johnson as he took the oath, and when the plane carried her husband’s body back to Washington. 

Those present later said she wanted people to see what had been done.

The photographs from that afternoon became among the most recognized images of the twentieth century. 

They showed the transfer of power and the immediate cost of the violence. 

More than sixty years later the pink suit remains a stark record of the day the country changed, and of the woman who chose not to erase the evidence of what she had witnessed. 🙏🌹

Far-right commentator Laura Loomer, a close ally of President Donald Trump, has been accused of accepting payments from private clients to publish political posts on X without disclosing them, according to a Washington Post investigation published on November 7. Financial records reviewed by the Post show four payments totaling more than $60,000 sent to Loomer and her company, King Breaker Media, since May 2025, though the documents do not state their purpose. Two sources said they paid Loomer directly and a third said they oversaw clients who did, with two saying she charged $3,000 to $5,000 per post. Loomer has 1.9 million followers on X.

Former Trump campaign adviser Alex Bruesewitz told the Post he paid Loomer for policy-related posts in 2025 through his consulting firm, X Strategies, and said such paid posts should be clearly disclosed. Conservative activist Jacob Engels also said he paid her and offered to share receipts and the names of others who did. Sources said Loomer's access to Trump made her an effective way for clients to get messages to the White House. Trump has previously acknowledged acting on some of her personnel recommendations. The White House declined to comment.

Loomer denied being paid to post, describing herself as a journalist and activist who does consulting and opposition research. She said Bruesewitz paid her to produce a one-page research document that he then asked her to share, and said she does not charge $5,000 per post. About an hour after speaking with the Post, she announced a break from her podcast, which she said was previously planned. Federal rules do not currently require influencers to disclose payments for political posts, and the allegations have renewed calls for greater transparency.

Me: The Quantum Self: Human Nature and Consciousness Defined by the New Physics

Ai: The Quantum Self: Human Nature and Consciousness Defined by the New Physics by Danah Zohar, published in 1990, is an ambitious exploration of the relationship between quantum physics, human consciousness, psychology, philosophy, and spirituality. Written in collaboration with Ian N. Marshall, the book proposes that the discoveries of modern physics may offer an entirely different way of understanding who we are and how we relate to the universe.
At the heart of the book is the idea that the human self should not be understood as a fixed, isolated entity operating within a mechanical universe. Instead, Zohar draws upon the principles of quantum mechanics to imagine consciousness and identity as dynamic, interconnected, and continuously evolving. She challenges the traditional scientific picture of human beings as essentially biological machines, suggesting that reality is far more fluid, relational, and participatory than classical physics once assumed.
The book explores several profound questions: What is consciousness? How does the mind relate to the physical body? Is the self something independent, or does it emerge through relationships with other people and the surrounding world? Could the interconnectedness described by quantum physics offer a new understanding of empathy, creativity, free will, and human identity?

Among its central themes are:
Quantum consciousness: Exploring whether quantum processes can provide a different framework for understanding the origins and nature of consciousness.
Mind and body: Challenging the conventional separation between mental experience and physical matter.
Quantum identity: Reconsidering the self as something fluid, interconnected, and constantly developing.
Human relationships: Examining how interconnectedness might transform our understanding of intimacy, empathy, and human connection.
Free will and creativity: Considering human beings as active participants in shaping their experiences and the world around them.
Quantum spirituality: Exploring possible connections between modern physics, the nature of existence, and spiritual questions about consciousness and the universe.
One of the book's most intriguing propositions is that human beings are not merely passive observers of reality but participants in its unfolding. This perspective encourages a more holistic understanding of existence, in which individuality and interconnectedness are not necessarily opposing ideas.

Intellectual significance
The Quantum Self belongs to an influential tradition of books attempting to bridge modern physics with philosophical and spiritual questions. It extends the kind of interdisciplinary inquiry found in Fritjof Capra's The Tao of Physics, bringing quantum ideas into discussions of psychology, personal identity, and human relationships.
It is important to distinguish Zohar's philosophical interpretations from established scientific conclusions: quantum mechanics does not, by itself, demonstrate that consciousness creates reality or that the universe possesses a mind.

Ultimately, The Quantum Self is an invitation to reconsider the nature of human existence. It challenges the mechanistic worldview and presents an alternative vision of the individual as an interconnected, creative, and evolving expression of a much larger universe.
It is particularly interesting for readers exploring consciousness studies, quantum philosophy, neuroscience, metaphysics, Eastern and Western philosophical traditions, and the relationship between science and spirituality.
Bibliographic note: Originally published by William Morrow in 1990; Ian N. Marshall collaborated on the book.

🧬 Researchers at Stanford and the Arc Institute introduced Germinal Multi, an AI method that jointly optimizes one antibody paratope against multiple antigen variants.

In two experimental campaigns, the authors report successful binders and neutralizers after screening only 57–60 designs per campaign.

🔬 A de novo antibody, R50, neutralized the historically distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants BA.2 and KP.3, with IC₅₀ values of 230 and 120 ng/mL. It also bound held-out evolutionary intermediates and the later variant PG.3.1, with a reported apparent Kᴅ of 26 nM.

For EGFR, 4 of 60 designs bound wild-type EGFR; collectively, those hits also recognized all 6 tested cetuximab-resistance variants.

🎯 The team also redesigned the broadly neutralizing antibody BD55-1205 against XFG-Next, an engineered escape variant guided by viral-evolution forecasts. Lead X51 neutralized both parental XFG and XFG-Next, at IC₅₀ values of 2.1 and 6.3 ng/mL.

Why it matters: instead of separately optimizing antibodies against one antigen at a time, multi-target design may offer a route to breadth across specified—and even held-out—variants.

⚠️ bioRxiv preprint only. Kᴅ values are apparent BLI measurements; neutralization used pseudovirus, not authentic virus or clinical studies. XFG-Next is an engineered challenge variant, and the linked Germinal Multi repository is currently empty.

🚨 VIRGINIA PARENTS FACE CRIMINAL CHARGES AFTER PARTY FOR 13-YEAR-OLD DRAWS UP TO 300 PEOPLE — BUT THEY SAY HIGH SCHOOLERS CRASHED IT

A McLean couple could face up to a year in jail after a backyard gathering intended for 10–20 middle school students spiraled into a neighborhood disturbance involving as many as 300 people.

Lisa Vaughan, 45, and Aubrey Vaughan, 55, have been charged with contributing to the delinquency of a minor and maintaining a common nuisance following the November 6 incident.

But the parents are disputing the police account.

▪️ THE PARTY: The Vaughans say their two 13-year-old sons invited classmates over, with bags and alcohol explicitly prohibited.

▪️ WHAT WENT WRONG: Their attorney says the invitation spread through social media and reached local high school students, who allegedly showed up uninvited.

▪️ POLICE RESPONSE: Officers arrived around 9 p.m. after multiple 911 calls and encountered a crowd of 100–300 people, fireworks and reports of underage drinking.

▪️ THE DEFENSE: Attorney Alaric Piette says the parents tried to keep strangers out, cooperated with responding officers and offered to let police inspect the party area.

▪️ THE CONSEQUENCES: Both parents surrendered voluntarily and were released on $1,000 unsecured bonds. Each faces two misdemeanor charges.

Fairfax County Police Chief Kevin Davis called large teen parties “universally a bad idea,” warning that even well-intentioned parents can lose control.

The case presents a difficult accountability question: If parents genuinely attempted to supervise a small gathering and uninvited teenagers overwhelmed their property, where should criminal responsibility begin and end?

And why have no charges been announced against the uninvited participants?

The Vaughans are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

🔊 Can Indigenous Knowledge Help Quiet Our Oceans? 🌊

Rising underwater noise from shipping, drilling, and sonar is disrupting marine ecosystems that rely on sound to survive.

In the latest issue of the International Journal for Underwater Domain Awareness (IJUDA, Vol. 01, 2026), our explore how traditional wisdom can complement modern acoustic science in their paper, "A Synergistic Approach to Underwater Noise Management: Integrating Indigenous Knowledge and Acoustic Science."

Key takeaways:

🔹 Beyond Tech: Generational coastal observations of species migration and behaviour offer vital ecological insights that acoustic tools alone can miss.

🔹 Global vs. Local: Unlike collaborative Arctic models in Canada, India’s coastal fishers—such as in Chilika Lagoon—hold rich ecological knowledge still underutilized in maritime policy.

🔹 Active Partnerships: Sustainable ocean governance requires engaging local communities as active knowledge partners, not passive stakeholders.

At the @MRCPune, we bridge underwater acoustic science with community stewardship through our Underwater Domain Awareness (#UDA) framework and IJUDA.MRC Summer intern Diya Rao Jaini from Keble College,University of Oxford (Alumni St.Stephen’s College,Delhi University) and our Publication and Research Head J. Cathrine

In his memoir, Thunder Below!, Commander Eugene Fluckey recounts that when he called for volunteers to go ashore at Karafuto (Sakhalin Island) to blow up a coastal Japanese supply train, the Japanese POW being held aboard the submarine stepped forward to volunteer for the sabotage mission.
In late June 1945, after sinking a Japanese trawler, the Barb pulled a Japanese sailor from the water. Like Yasujiro Kitamura on the earlier patrol, this prisoner was treated well by the crew and quickly grew friendly with the Americans.
When word spread through the boat in July 1945 that Fluckey was assembling an eight-man landing party to row ashore and plant demolition charges on the railroad tracks, almost the entire crew volunteered—including the Japanese prisoner.
The prisoner eagerly asked to join the shore party and promised Commander Fluckey that he would not try to escape.
Fluckey declined the offer. He selected eight American sailors based on specific criteria, including being unmarried and having Boy Scout training for outdoor survival and first aid.
The name of this Japanese sailor is not known.

text:
This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here.

Last week, MIT Technology Review held its inaugural EmTech Digital conference in London. It was a great success! I loved seeing so many of you there asking excellent questions, and it was a couple of days full of brain-tickling insights about where AI is going next. 

Here are the three main things I took away from the conference.

1. AI avatars are getting really, really good

UK-based AI unicorn Synthesia teased its next generation of AI avatars, which are far more emotive and realistic than any I have ever seen before. The company is pitching these avatars as a new, more engaging way to communicate. Instead of skimming through pages and pages of onboarding material, for example, new employees could watch a video where a hyperrealistic AI avatar explains what they need to know about their job. This has the potential to change the way we communicate, allowing content creators to outsource their work to custom avatars and making it easier for organizations to share information with their staff. 

2. AI agents are coming 

Thanks to the ChatGPT boom, many of us have interacted with  an AI assistant that can retrieve information. But the next generation of these tools, called AI agents, can do much more than that. They are AI models and algorithms that can autonomously make decisions by themselves in a dynamic world. Imagine an AI travel agent that can not only retrieve information and suggest things to do, but also take action to book things for you, from flights to tours and accommodations. Every AI lab worth its salt, from OpenAI to Meta to startups, is racing to build agents that can reason better, memorize more steps, and interact with other apps and websites.  

3. Humans are not perfect either 

One of the best ways we have of ensuring that AI systems don’t go awry is getting humans to audit and evaluate them. But humans are complicated and biased, and we don’t always get things right. In order to build machines that meet our expectations​ and complement our limitations, we should account for human error from the get-go. In a fascinating presentation, Katie Collins, an AI researcher at the University of Cambridge, explained how she found that allowing people to express how certain or uncertain they are—for example, by using a percentage to indicate how confident they are in labeling data—leads to better accuracy for AI models overall. The only downside with this approach is that it costs more and takes more time.

And we’re doing it all again next month, this time at the mothership. 

Join us for EmTech Digital at the MIT campus in Cambridge, Massachusetts, on May 22-23, 2024. I’ll be there—join me! 

Our fantastic speakers include Nick Clegg, president of global affairs at Meta, who will talk about elections and AI-generated misinformation. We also have the OpenAI researchers who built the video-generation AI Sora, sharing their vision on how generative AI will change Hollywood. Then Max Tegmark, the MIT professor who wrote an open letter last year calling for a pause on AI development, will take stock of what has happened and discuss how to make powerful systems more safe. We also have a bunch of top scientists from the labs at Google, OpenAI, AWS, MIT, Nvidia and more. 

Readers of The Algorithm get 30% off with the discount code ALGORITHMD24.

I hope to see you there!

Now read the rest of The Algorithm

Deeper Learning

Researchers taught robots to run. Now they’re teaching them to walk.

Researchers at Oregon State University have successfully trained a humanoid robot called Digit V3 to stand, walk, pick up a box, and move it from one location to another. Meanwhile, a separate group of researchers from the University of California, Berkeley, have focused on teaching Digit to walk in unfamiliar environments while carrying different loads, without toppling over. 

What’s the big deal: Both groups are using an AI technique called sim-to-real reinforcement learning, a burgeoning method of training two-legged robots like Digit. Researchers believe it will lead to more robust, reliable two-legged machines capable of interacting with their surroundings more safely—as well as learning much more quickly. Read more from Rhiannon Williams. 

Bits and Bytes

It’s time to retire the term “user”
The proliferation of AI means we need a new word. Tools we once called AI bots have been assigned lofty titles like “copilot,” “assistant,” and “collaborator” to convey a sense of partnership instead of a sense of automation. But if AI is now a partner, then what are we? (MIT Technology Review) 

Three ways the US could help universities compete with tech companies on AI innovation
Empowering universities to remain at the forefront of AI research will be key to realizing the field’s long-term potential, argue Ylli Bajraktari, Tom Mitchell, and Daniela Rus. (MIT Technology Review) 

AI was supposed to make police body cams better. What happened?
New AI programs that analyze bodycam recordings promise more transparency but are doing little to change culture. This story serves as a useful reminder that technology is never a panacea for these sorts of deep-rooted issues. (MIT Technology Review) 

The World Health Organization’s AI chatbot makes stuff up
The World Health Organization launched a “virtual health worker“ to help people with questions about things like mental health, tobacco use, and healthy eating. But the chatbot frequently offers outdated information or just simply makes things up, a common issue with AI models. This is a great cautionary tale of why it’s not always a good idea to use AI chatbots. Hallucinating chatbots can lead to serious consequences when they are applied to important tasks such as giving health advice. (Bloomberg) 

Meta is adding AI assistants everywhere in its biggest AI push
The tech giant is rolling out its latest AI model, Llama 3, in most of its apps including Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp. People will also be able to ask its AI assistants for advice, or use them to search for information on the internet. (New York Times) 

Stability AI is in trouble
One of the first new generative AI unicorns, the company behind the open-source image-generating AI model Stable Diffusion, is laying off 10% of its workforce. Just a couple of weeks ago its CEO, Emad Mostaque, announced that he was leaving the company. Stability has also lost several high-profile researchers and struggled to monetize its product, and it is facing a slew of lawsuits over copyright. (The Verge)

An individual, partnership, corporation, association, or any other nongovernmental entity shall not operate for the direct or indirect purpose, in whole or in part, of referring potential clients to attorneys, and no attorney shall accept a referral of such potential clients, unless all of the following requirements are met:

(1) The service is certified by the State Bar of California and is operated in conformity with minimum standards for a lawyer referral service established by the State Bar and approved by the Supreme Court.

(2) The combined charges to the potential client by the referral service and the attorney to whom the potential client is referred do not exceed the total cost that the client would normally pay if no referral service were involved.

https://t.co/pMjDObsz0c

A. Petition for H-1B Nonimmigrant Worker by a small nonprofit is $460 (8 CFR §106.2(a)(3)(i)). Total is $960 including Fraud Prevention and Detection Fees.

B. Petition for O Nonimmigrant Worker with 1 to 25 named beneficiaries: $1,055¹ (8 CFR §106.2(a)(3)(vii)).

¹ Under 8 CFR § 106.2(a)(3)(ix), an exception is authorized "For small nonprofits" as defined in 8 CFR § 106.1(f), reducing the fee for O-1 classification to one-half the standard amount rounded to the nearest $5 increment, making the total filing cost $530.

Fifth, although "dual intent" is permissible for O-1 and residence abroad is not required, applicants must still overcome the presumption of immigrant intent.

Moreover, DHS did not propose a minimum investment amount for beneficiary owners and did not add one through the New Final Rule 88 FR 75191, effective January 17, 2025.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

Jan-March 2026
Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

AI is helping organizations in nearly every industry increase productivity, engage customers, realize operational efficiencies, and gain a competitive edge. Advances in supercomputing in the cloud and the ability to achieve processing at an exascale level are major catalysts for this new era of AI innovation.

Common AI use cases today include personalized healthcare and targeted therapies, virtual assistants and chatbots, financial fraud detection, predictive maintenance, autonomous cars and machinery, energy management, and accelerated scientific discoveries.

Some companies are deep into their AI journey, delivering advanced AI-enabled products and services, but many businesses are at the early stages and are struggling with where and how to best apply AI in their business. AI is complex, requiring new skills, tools, and technologies.

To accelerate AI development and integration, organizations can benefit from a trusted partner that has AI expertise across the complete technology stack. The right AI solution provider can help determine the best AI strategy for a company’s specific business model and provide comprehensive, unified services, advanced infrastructure, and tools specifically designed for AI.

Discover the latest AI technologies. Join Microsoft at the NVIDIA GTC AI Conference March 18–21. Learn more.   

Companies across the world are turning to Microsoft to help them transform their business with innovative, secure, and responsible AI. At the forefront of artificial intelligence, Microsoft has delivered cutting-edge advances in vision, speech, language, decision-making, machine learning, and supercomputing infrastructure for more than 30 years. Hear how Microsoft AI solutions are helping organizations around the world achieve more in the video below.

Accelerating AI application development

Microsoft recently unveiled yet another round of AI services that can help businesses accelerate AI production, whether by adding intelligence to existing applications and processes or creating new ones from scratch. These new services include the following:

  • Azure AI Studio, now in preview, empowers organizations and developers to innovate with AI. The platform, accessibly and responsibly designed, provides a one-stop shop for developers to seamlessly explore, build, test, and deploy AI solutions using state-of-the-art AI tools and machine learning models, all grounded in responsible AI practices. Developers can build generative AI applications, including copilot experiences, using out-of-the-box and customizable tooling and models with built-in security and compliance.
  • Azure OpenAI Service offers industry-leading coding and language AI models and the latest advancements in generative AI for content creation, conversational AI, and data grounding.
  • New GPT-4 Turbo in Azure OpenAI provides a leap forward with lower pricing, extended prompt length, and structured JSON formatting, delivering improved efficiency and control.
  • GPT-4 Turbo with Vision is a new large multimodal model (LMM) developed by OpenAI that can analyze images and videos and provide textual responses to questions about them.
  • DALL·E 3 is the latest image generation model from OpenAI, featuring enhanced image quality, more complex scenes, improved performance when rendering text in images, and more aspect ratio options.

Powering AI workloads

Microsoft is also reimagining every aspect of their data centers to deliver the agility, power, scalability, and efficiencies AI workloads demand. Microsoft’s pioneering performance for AI has ranked them as the number-one cloud in the Top500 List of the world’s supercomputers and powered innovations like a new battery material. AI trailblazers are building and training the most sophisticated models in the world on Microsoft Azure AI infrastructure.

Here are some of Microsoft’s latest infrastructure advancements:

  • Custom-built silicon tailored for the Microsoft cloud offers optimized performance for AI and enterprise workloads. Azure Maia, an AI accelerator chip, is specifically designed to run cloud-based training and inferencing for AI workloads, such as OpenAI models, Bing, GitHub Copilot, and ChatGPT. Azure Cobalt is a cloud-native chip optimized for performance, power efficiency, and cost-effectiveness.
  • New Azure Boost enables greater network and storage performance at scale, improves security, and reduces servicing impact for specialized AI clusters or  general-purpose compute workloads.
  • Microsoft copilot for Azure simplifies operations and management with an AI companion that can help users design, operate, optimize, and troubleshoot infrastructure from cloud to edge.
  • New Azure NC H100 v5 virtual machine series built with NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPUs provide greater memory per GPU, increasing performance for mid-range AI training and generative AI inferencing. Microsoft will also add the latest NVIDIA H200 Tensor Core GPU to its fleet to support larger model inferencing with no increase in latency.
  • NVIDIA AI foundry service supercharges the development and tuning of custom generative AI applications for enterprises and startups deploying on Microsoft Azure.

Experience these advancements at NVIDIA GTC

Companies can experience Microsoft’s latest AI services and technologies and learn how to power their AI transformation at the NVIDIA GTC AI Conference March 18 to 21 in San Jose, California (and virtually). Through in-person and on-demand sessions, live discussions, and hands-on training, attendees will

  • Get to know the core Azure AI services and technologies that power some of the world’s largest and most complex AI models and applications.
  • Discover how to accelerate the delivery of generative AI and large language models (LLMs).
  • Explore how Azure AI studio and purpose-built cloud infrastructure can accelerate AI development and deployment.
  • Learn from best practices and customer experiences to speed AI production.

text:
Happy Birthday Veronica Lake

Lake was one of the most glamorous leading ladies of the 1940s, famous for her blonde peek-a-boo hairstyle that was copied by millions of women around the world. Specialising in femme fatale roles, she is best remembered for her pairings with Alan Ladd. Lake was born Constance Ockelman in 1922 in Brooklyn. She had a troubled childhood and was diagnosed with schizophrenia, which augured ill for the future. The family moved to California, where she attracted the attention of producer Arthur Hornblow Jr., who was looking for a girl to play a nightclub singer in “I Wanted Wings” (1941). Hornblow changed her name to Veronica Lake, and the film made the teenager a star overnight. During filming, her long hair accidentally fell over her right eye and created a "peek-a-boo" effect. "I had my arm on a table ... it slipped ... and my hair – it was always baby fine and had this natural break – fell over my face ... It became my trademark", she recalled. Lake was then cast in Preston Sturges's “Sullivan's Travels” with Joel McCrea. The usually amiable actor loathed working with her and vowed never to do it again. This was followed by the film noir “This Gun for Hire” (1942) with Robert Preston and Alan Ladd. Her scenes with Ladd were electrifying, prompting Paramount to reteam them in “The Glass Key” Lake then made the comedy “I Married a Witch” with Fredric March, who also detested her, saying she ground her knee into his crotch during love scenes. Both films were highly successful, and when the United States entered World War II, Lake traveled the country raising money for war bonds. She made an appearance in Paramount's musical revue “Star Spangled Rhythm”, performing "A Sweater, Sarong and a Peek-A-Boo Bang" with Paulette Goddard and Dorothy Lamour, and co-starred in “So Proudly We Hail!” (1943), receiving acclaim for her portrayal of a suicidal nurse. Despite her success, Lake suffered a series of setbacks that ultimately destroyed her. Her complex personality led to a reputation for being difficult. Worse, on “Sullivan's Travels”, Lake had omitted to disclose that she was six months pregnant, upsetting Preston Sturges to the extent that he had to be physically restrained. Eddie Bracken was quoted as saying, "She was known as 'The Bitch' and she deserved the title." Yet “I Married A Witch” director, René Clair liked her: “She was a very gifted girl, but she didn't believe she was gifted.” Grace Kelly, who had a friend who knew Lake, commented, “She was terribly insecure and needed constant praise.” In late 1943, Lake took time off after giving birth to a son who died while still in hospital. She filed for divorce from her husband and began drinking heavily. Upon returning to work, Lake was cast in the film noir “The Blue Dahlia” (1946), with Alan Ladd, who had become one of Paramount's top stars. Her performance failed to impress screenwriter Raymond Chandler, who referred to her as "Moronica Lake". It was, however, a box office success. She then starred in the Western “Ramrod” (1947), but after a series of flops, Paramount dropped her. Bankrupt and on the verge of a nervous breakdown, the former star drifted between cheap hotels in New York, and was arrested for drunkenness and disorderly conduct. In 1962, a reporter found her working as a waitress in a cocktail lounge, under the name "Connie de Toth". After the story ran, fans of Lake sent her money which she returned as "a matter of pride". Her memoirs, “Veronica: The Autobiography of Veronica Lake”, were published in 1970. When she visited the UK to promote the book, she received an offer to play Blanche DuBois in a revival of “A Streetcar Named Desire”, and her performance was widely praised. Her final film was “Flesh Feast” a low-budget horror movie. In 1973, Lake returned to America complaining of stomach pains. She was diagnosed with cirrhosis of the liver; the result of years of drinking. Veronica Lake died on July 7, 1973, aged 50.

text:
I offered to make her something similar at home, but she kept saying nothing else sounded good and she’d rather not eat at all.

Eventually, I gave in.

It took me about 45 minutes to get there, another 25 minutes waiting for the food, and nearly an hour driving back.

I ended up using half a personal day because there was no way I’d make it back to work on time. Now I have to pick up an extra shift next week to cover it.

And it’s not just that one incident.

My wife stays home, and since getting pregnant, her sleeping schedule has been all over the place. She’s usually awake late at night and sleeps quite a bit during the day.

Lately, she’ll wake me up around 3 a.m. because she’s hungry.

I don’t mind getting her something, but half the time she doesn’t even know what she wants.

We’ll spend 20 or 30 minutes going through different options before she finally decides. Then I’m either cooking or getting dressed to drive somewhere.

By the time I get back into bed, I’m lucky if I get another couple hours of sleep before my alarm goes off at 6:30.

It’s starting to affect me at work. I’m tired, easily irritated, and struggling to concentrate.

I love my wife, and I understand she’s going through a lot physically. I’m not expecting her to just ignore her cravings.

But I also feel like being supportive shouldn’t mean running myself into the ground.

I’m thinking about sitting her down this weekend and explaining that we need to find a better way to handle this.

Would I be wrong for telling my pregnant wife that I can’t keep doing all of this?

text:
The seventh year of Hogwarts at least so far, was a sort of twisted irony for Neville.  While it was true that the Carrows were Death-eaters, their stalking of the halls of the school provided the best entertainment Neville ever experienced.  Clearly they were dangerous and enthusiastic in what they claimed to be ‘discipline’, but their competency was constantly challenged by what remained of Dumbedore’s Army.
Things started slowly, with many of the students unwilling to risk the brutality of the new disciplinary administrators. Several students were sent to the infirmary for several days to recover from the injuries they suffered, which regularly included broken bones and lost teeth. Things were looking like they would fall apart out of fear alone in less than a month, but help arrived in the form of Seamus and Daphne.
Seamus’ talents at sabotage and guerilla warfare resulted in several victories against the Carrows that the others couldn’t ignore, the greatest being his miraculous delivery of some sort of pepper bomb  across a corridor and down a spiral flight of stairs which completely disabled the Death-Eaters and allowed a student to escape their clutches.  After that, people started coming back to the DA, and not just Gryffindors.  Hufflepuffs, and Ravenclaws trickled in over the course of several months and the noted clandestine support of Slytherin was instrumental in their activities.  While none save Daphne walked into the Room of Requirment, students were regularly arriving with information provided by friends and informants
As for Daphne, she would only show up once a month to speak privately to Seamus, then leave without a word to anyone else. Whatever she told him always gave their expert saboteur new motivation and a burst of wicked creativity. So motivated was he that it took a week to convince him to not blow up the bridge leading up to the castle out of what he called ‘patriotic pride.’
By the third month, Neville, and Luna were practically living in the Room, it being too dangerous for them to walk outside without suffering the wrath of the Carrows. Seamus was advised multiple times to slow down his activities but getting him to stay -in- the room was more difficult than shoving an angry cat into a wet paper bag.  Only when he was injured or Daphne came to visit did he show up and stay for any notable time period.
It wasn’t a perfect experience. Both Seamus and Neville were captured several times, with Seamus catching the brunt of the reprisal from both of the death-eaters.  Not permitted to kill him, they certainly tried their best to make him wish he were dead.  Both him and Neville proved to be impossible to torture into submission, with one particular torture session having them both there as an impotent means of intimidating the other. Instead they just laughed and joked the whole time until McGonagall intervened.
It turned out that Seamus and Neville worked well together, nearly perfect sides of the same coin.  While Seamus was the perfect operator and planner, Neville was a natural leader, capable of motivating even the most injured or depressed of students with only a brief conversation.  With their efforts, it became nearly impossible for the Carrows to do their job effectively, and several classes were so disrupted that they were cancelled for days.  When the holidays finally arrived, nearly all of the DA managed to escape out of a recently discovered path that led directly to Hogsmeade and return to their families. Only Seamus and Neville remained behind.  

The two weeks of Christmas holiday were more than enough to distract him from the absence of Luna who had left to check in on her father. Day in, Day out they wreaked havoc in the school. Filling corridors with traps, placing hazardous plants in areas where the Carrows would patrol, and generally making a gigantic mess of the school.  They were so effective that they nearly killed Alecto with a clever mandrake contraption trap. Two weeks however, goes by quickly when you are trying to eliminate Death-Eaters using mundane tools, and the boys found themselves standing on the train platform in Hogsmeade, waiting for the express to arrive.
“Can you believe that Alecto Carrow wears earplugs when he sleeps? Talk about bad luck!” said Seamus with a laugh, “I really thought we had the bastard that time too! I have to pay him back for my shoulder blade he dislocated.”
Neville grinned, “Yeah but it works in our favor. Now they don’t leave their rooms without earplugs in which gives us a huge advantage.  If we can apply more pressure we may even make them leave the school strictly out of fear of their own safety.  Did you leave the present for Amycus?”
Semus gave a thumbs up.  Carefully transfigured pepper bombs were glued under her teachers chair, set to go off in a few days exactly when her class would begin, with her sitting in it.  More than enough to disrupt her ‘Defense against the dark arts’ class for at least a day. the 'pepper' was something Neville provided, the dried and powdered fruit of a plant that even dragons avoided.
“Have you heard from Daphne?” asked Neville
Seamus shook his head, “She made it clear, no communications over Christmas.  They are too busy and her father is constantly being visited by Death Eaters trying to get him to join their ranks. I think they took a trip to Rome this year just to get away from them. What about Luna?”
“She sent a letter, which did nothing but worry me,” said Neville, offering a folded letter to Seamus, who unfolded it.
“‘I’m Sorry.’?  That doesn’t sound good.”
“Luna probably couldn’t tell me more due to the constant surveillance on her Dad, but that has kept me up at night for a week,” Said Neville with a deep sigh.
“Don’t worry, mate.  She will be on that train and we can get back to it with full beautiful blonde support!” Said Seamus, slapping his hand on his friend's back.

Before Neville could respond, Seamus pointed into the distance, the enormous and beautiful steam locomotive puffed into view, leaving great plumes of hot steam in the cold winter air. They said nothing until the great train arrived and stopped, students disembarking from the train with far less of the jovial and energetic feel that they had come to expect from the moment.  Their eyes scanned around, searching for just the right blonde.
“I don’t see Luna.” Said Neville, worried.
“There’s Daphne!” Seamus exclaimed.
Daphne walked up with the full confidence and authority of someone who didn’t just own the Hogwarts Express, but the entirety of Hogsmeade.  Far less than greet Seamus, she strode foreword and pulled her wand from her pocket, knocking him aside with a sweeping wave of her arm. Her golden eyes flashed with disgust and her voice hissed, “Out of my way, Mudblood!" before striding on towards the school.
Seamus staggered performatively, then moved back to Neville as they waited, and waited, and waited.  Luna never emerged from the train and the conductor insisted that no students were aboard.  Neville stood and stared at the rails, his face seeming to turn to stone as he turned on his heel and walked back to Hogsmeade with Seamus in tow.  In the crush of students they made their way to the Hogs Head where the tunnel to the Room was, never speaking until they arrived safely.
“She wasn’t there.” Neville said dowerly.
“Hold on, before you get all mopey on me.” Said Seamus, pulling out a small locket from his robes, it glittered spectacularly with carefully inset gems that were grass green in color. With a flick he opened it to show a beautiful and tiny portrait of Daphne, smiling with her authoritarian grin.  With a flick of his wand, the portrait began to move and speak much like the magical portraits that were common in the school. Her voice though was filled with concern, which was something Neville never thought he would hear. 
“Seamus. Luna was on the train, but right after she sat down in her car she passed out. The conductor tried to wake her up, but nothing would do the job. We were all worried she had been poisoned but then the Death-eaters showed up and took her.  I don’t know where, but they didn’t know why she was unconscious either. They said strange magic was involved.  Please be safe.”
“That’s a clever thing.” Neville said, impressed at the locket
Seamus blushed a bit, “She gave it to me for Christmas before she left.”
Neville nodded, “Something happened to her, before she ever got on the Hogwarts Express, now she is in the hands of the Death-Eaters… Do you think the Carrows are involved?”
Seamus took a moment to think before shrugging, “Who knows.  We don’t know where she is, or where they are taking her.  Lets just be glad they wanted her alive.”
Neville stared down at the floor in silence for several long minutes before looking up at his friend, “I think it’s time we both tell the truth about ourselves.”
“I’m sorry?” Said Seamus
“They have Luna. No amount of philosophy or motivation will stop me from getting her back, but in order to do that I need to know that leaving the school is possible.  I know something bad is happening under the school, it’s been going on for years and you are involved.  I cannot plan to break her free unless I have more information and I don't think it's safe for me to leave the castle right now.”
Seamus stared dumbfounded at Neville, “I mean… Neville you can leave any time–”
“Can I?  I don’t think I can.  Something tells me that if I do, things may become irredeemably bad. I am also sick of keeping the secret for this long. I either tell you, or I go attack the Ministry again until someone gets lucky and kills me. I am not a rational actor right now, Seamus.”
Seamus opened and closed his mouth a few times before sitting on one of the old cots in the room, pulling out and opening bottle of butterbeer he got at the Hogs Head and taking a long draw of the bottle.
“Start talkin’ then. The least I can do is keep you alive.”

As assignments go, this one was clearly the worst. Most low level Death Eaters would be thrilled at basic guard duty, as it has few risks involved. The dungeons under the Ministry of Magic were very well equipped, the walls were thick and every cell door was heavily warded for every conceivable form of magic. None of that made Bonsley feel better about his safety with what was inside the cell.  When told by his superiors to retrieve the Lovegood girl, it was a simple enough task; Apparate, threaten to kill the conductor, find the girl, leave.  She even had the good sense to already be unconscious at the time which avoided any messy entanglements like dead children.
Then things got weird.
Vicks went in first to give her food and to ‘check on her vitals’, which was his own private code for something far worse.  He went into the room alone with her food and a grin, and never came out again.  When the room was opened some thirty minutes later there was just the blonde teenager laying on the cell bed, not a single sign of Vicks or his food tray.  Magics were used to scour the room but it was as if he never crossed the threshold of the door.
Then Wedge went in, a large and violent man insistent on beating her into consciousness to figure out what happened to his best friend.  After the doors slammed shut behind him the sounds of his footsteps could be heard. First, confident steps towards the bed, then a pause, then sudden frantic movement.  There were no screams, though something huge and heavy seemed to hit the heavy metal door with enough force to liquify a human.  When the door was opened, the only evidence that Wedge was there was a thin coating of dripping red painted across two thirds of the room with not a drop falling on the girl.
After that, they went in force into the room, picking her up and moving her to a different cell, figuring something was going on with the room, possibly a curse of some kind, and tried again. Nothing seemed to happen, though she would not rouse, even for food.  Water had to be poured into her mouth to keep her hydrated and a very grumpy witch was ordered to deal with sanitary issues.
Despite all of this, she never seemed to starve. Her body simply lay limp and motionless in what seemed like an eternal sleep.  Their medical experts checked her, commenting that there was some sort of magic they had never seen before, but she was somehow healthy and alive.
Then the dreams came to Bonsley.  Every night after sleep he would dream of being alone in a black void, the only visible thing being a golden statue of a girl wrapped in the darkness. He ran towards it, but any time he would get close enough to touch it, the darkness spawned endless hungry eyes and teeth which came for him.  Waking up in cold sweats was getting old, and several requests to be set off to do other work were constantly rejected.
Another night and another shift came.  Sawyer was at the door standing to attention as he walked up to greet him.
“Evenin`, anything happen during your shift?” Bonsley asked as he pulled out a box of cigarettes, lighting one and taking a long drag.
“Nah.  A few torches went out down the corridor but beyond that things were quiet. Potts took the day off, said something about hearing something in the walls.”
“In the walls? They’re solid stone. That coward just wanted the day off.”
“Can ya blame him after what happened to Lee?” said Sawyer, “They only found the left eye.”
“Lousy ministry cells have curses on them designed to disappear people.  To think they would claim some sort of moral authority when they do this crap behind closed doors.” said Bonsley with a cackle.
“Pretty dang clever though, gonna have to figure out how they did it, though I don’t know why it hasn’t off’d the girl.” Sawyer said
“Probably restrictions, can’t kill someone underage or something stupid like that. The Ministry had no consistency with its morality.  I have come to figure that they were just like us, but less honest.”
Bonsley offered Sawyer a cigarette, but his hand didn’t move from his side, a bit strange since Sawyer was a chain smoker, but he shrugged and pulled another long drag from the cigarette before talking, “I hate this job, been getting nightmares every night since we moved her cell and I can barely sleep now.”
“M-Me to.” Said Sawyer with an odd stutter, “I keep seeing something waiting behind the walls, it even started to say my name.”
“I see some golden statue wrapped in darkness, then it’s just all eyes and teeth.” Bonsley chuckled, “really stupid when you think of it,”
“No.. It’s not stupid, because he is actually moving closë̦̏r to me” Sawyer said with another shudder.  There was something odd about his voice, a sort of double-voice or flanging effect
“Sawyer, you gotta lay off the good stuff, Lord Voldemort isn’t coming here, he is holed up at the Malfoy’s place. There is no reason for him to show his face in a dump like this.” Bonsley said waving his hand.
“No– Not Voldemort.  He who waits behind the wall. I think he is c͖̈́o̰̽̚m̜̀̃ì͙̒n̞̆̒g̪͊̌,” Said Sawyer, when the final word came from his mouth, there was a strange distant rumbling behind it.
Bonsley began to sweat, something was clearly not right with Sawyer, “Hey man, are you alright? You are shaking.”
The hooded figure of Sawyer suddenly went rigid, then relaxed, the facemask all Death Eaters wear falling to the floor as a voice that shook Bonsley’s bones uttered from under the hood, “H͔͋͒ͅĘ͖͔̯͋̎̃͋ C̵̨͙̬̰͚͒̍̀̏̐́O̞͕͎̰̦̫̪̺̽̑̐͛̒̽̂̕M̵̛͉̟̳͖̻̦͔̮͉̽̉͆̆̈̽̏͑̽̂Ę̷͍͇͖̮̰̟̮̰̯̣̙̜̈̇͂̊̽̑̈̽̍̎̈̚ͅS̴̨͚̰̘̳̭͖̘͉̱͎̔̿̋̔͑͆̏͒!̨̧̧̹̖̰̭̘̯̘͙̞̠͔̪̌̾͆̎͊̅̍̈̏͐̋̑͘”
The face was warped, fissures forming along every surface vertically as Sawyers eyes went pitch black,  The fissures weeped blood as they opened to reveal irregular teeth that began to part, revealing nothing but nondescript flesh and thousands of inhuman eyes that stared at Bonsley.
The sweat was pouring down his face, enough that he had to wipe his eyes clean only to see the crimson of his blood upon his gloved hand, his throat swelled and from it issued the last utterance before his ascension.

text:
@EricLDaugh: Thank you for letting everyone know about this interview with Secretary Scott Bessent. It is hard not to feel some trepidation after what happened in the Midterm Election. But thank you for posting this. It is very reassuring.

 We have seen President Trump's successes in addressing foreign Heads of State. For example, NATO members were not paying the required dues their countries had agreed to when they joined. They agreed to pay 5% of their GDP in annual dues, but they were paying only 1-2% of that amount. That left the United States to pay the shortfall, and the U.S. had been stuck with that bill for decades. (And all those billions of dollars have added to our National Debt and caused additional interest to be tacked on.) 

President Trump informed those leaders that not paying the full amount of their dues to NATO was no longer acceptable. As a result, European countries are now paying 5% of GDP, or very close to it. Many Presidents could have addressed this problem, but no one was willing to "take on the responsibility" of telling NATO countries to pay what they owed. This is only one example of the kinds of things President Trump has done to benefit our country. But you never hear about these kinds of things in the MSM. It might get a brief headline for one day, and then it is back to vilifying him for things that aren't even factual.

If he can 'take on' the Presidents, Premiers, and Prime Ministers of foreign countries and get them to pay billions of dollars they owed, it is NOT too surprising that a few Democrats, Republicans, or anyone else who might want to "give him an earful" would not get very far when they came to the Oval Office. That will be very comforting to think about over the next two years. He is a brilliant strategist, and it is laughable to read an article that tries to diagnose him in the early stages of dementia or any of the other medical conditions they try to saddle him with. 

It's really ironic when they say he is suffering from Alzheimer's because we observed Pres. Biden, who truly DID have a medical issue. We all saw it and knew it, but the MSM wouldn't even mention there could be a problem until 2 months before the 2024 election. They knew he was ill. He needed medical care, but the Media covered for him, and his wife and staff covered for him. It wasn't until his behavior and performance at the Presidential Debate made it impossible to deny  reality that they had to acknowledge he was ill. 

It was actually painful to watch President Biden during those years. I still have the image of him at a gathering in Europe. It was a G7 Summit. Everyone was outside standing in line as a group for a Photo-Op. But he suddenly wandered off to the right, where a skydiver had just landed. Prime Minister Meroni of Italy had the compassion to walk over to where he had gone. She took him by the arm and gently guided him back to the group for the photo.** 

That should have been a wake-up call that a serious problem needed to be addressed. But anything negative about President Biden was treated like the positive things about President Trump. If they were mentioned at all, it was a small headline for one day.
Thank you again for reminding us that President Trump has everything under control.  

**An interesting note: I wanted to verify my recollection of that event and what year it occurred. It was June 13, 2024. That was 4 1/2 months before the Election. I searched using AI through Chrome Gemini.  They are STILL covering for Joe Biden. The way it is written NOW is not what I SAW. It tells me my version is mistaken, and anyone who thought it seemed odd for him to do what he did is making a big deal out of nothing. He was simply and intentionally going over to offer his congratulations to the skydiver with a thumbs-up. But I will ask this. Does it seem appropriate to break away from a group of world leaders and leave them hanging while you shuffle off to congratulate a skydiver who was part of a planned exhibition?

A link showed that the New York Post, at that time, had reported the event exactly as I saw it. They were excoriated for printing such nonsense. The link says Meroni walked toward him and "signaled" him to come back to the group. That is not correct! She touched his arm and guided him back to the group for the photo. Doesn't that tell us we shouldn't blindly trust everything we read or learn from AI? 
It is only as good or as accurate as the database it pulls from, and that database is only as accurate as the programmer inputting the data. The data input may be influenced by the programmer's own ideology or political leanings, so how can we be sure we're getting facts and not someone's version of the facts? That is a big question that deserves attention, IMO.

text:
Hanin. Mother of two:

In Gaza, our daily life has become a battle. 💔

Everything is expensive—food, cooking gas, even firewood. 
If we manage to find a canister of cooking gas, the price is exorbitant; if we can’t find one, we have to cook over a fire—filling our lungs and our children’s eyes with smoke, just to prepare a single meal.

We live in tents that offer no protection from the cold or the rain. 
In the winter, the rain seeps in, our mattresses get soaked, and the children wake up cold and wet, with nothing to cover them. 
We huddle them together so they can keep each other warm, while we stay awake, terrified that the tent might flood or be blown away by the wind.

We aren’t truly living—we are merely trying to stay alive.

You're offered 4 life-changing beds, but they each cut a decade off your life. 

Bed 1: Every time you fall asleep, you enter a complete lucid dream where you have full control of reality. You could live as a billionaire, date your dream crush, or explore fictional universes. But you can't extend the length of your dream.

Bed 2: Every time you sleep in this bed, your body completely regenerates. You could cure terminal illnesses, regrow missing limbs, or recover from any injury overnight.

Bed 3: This bed allows you to travel to any point in human history while you're asleep. You could witness ancient civilizations, meet historical figures, or discover lost treasures. You can interact with the past, change historical events, and even bring objects back into the present.

Bed 4: Every time you fall asleep, you can choose to wake up anywhere in the universe. You could teleport to another country, explore distant planets, or instantly travel to galaxies billions of light-years away. You will be completely immortal, and can bring anything back when you wake up.

How many are you picking?

text:
☀️ Chhath Puja is an ancient four-day Vedic festival dedicated to Surya Dev (the Sun God) and Chhathi Maiya. In 2026, the main Kartika Chhath Puja is celebrated from November 13 to November 16 across Bihar, Jharkhand, eastern Uttar Pradesh, and Nepal. 🪷

✨ The Four Days of Chhath Puja:-
The festival involves strict discipline, purity, and a 36-hour waterless fast (nirjala vrat).

Day 1: Nahay Khay (Nov 13). Devotees take a holy bath in a river or water body and clean their homes to prepare for the festival. They eat a single sattvic meal consisting of bottle gourd (lauki), chana dal, and rice cooked in earthen or bronze utensils.

Day 2: Kharna (Nov 14). Observers keep a strict fast without food or water from sunrise to sunset. After sunset, they worship Mother Earth and break the fast with jaggery rice pudding (gur ka kheer), roti, and bananas before starting their 36-hour waterless fast.

Day 3: Sandhya Arghya (Nov 15). Devotees gather at riverbanks or ponds (ghats) with bamboo baskets (soop) filled with fruits, sugarcane, and thekua (a sweet wheat cookie). Standing waist-deep in water, they offer arghya (water and milk) to the setting sun.

Day 4: Usha Arghya (Nov 16). Before dawn, devotees return to the water to offer prayers and arghya to the rising sun. Once the ritual concludes, they break their 36-hour fast and share prasad with family and neighbors.

✨ Deeper Meanings and Secrets of the Festival:
Beyond its public rituals, Chhath Puja carries unique spiritual, scientific, and social significance outlined in cultural guides.

Worshipping the Setting Sun: Chhath is the only major festival that honors the setting sun alongside the rising sun. This symbolizes gratitude for completion and teaches that every decline is followed by a new beginning.
No Idols, Priests, or Temples: Unlike most Hindu festivals, Chhath requires no idols or Brahmin priests. Devotees connect directly with nature, making it a deeply egalitarian celebration where everyone stands side-by-side in the same water.
Natural Bio-Science and Detoxification: Standing in cool water during early morning and late afternoon exposes the body to low-angle sunlight. This specific sunlight maximizes safe Vitamin D absorption while the combination of water immersion and fasting helps detoxify the body and calm the nervous system.
100% Eco-Friendly Tradition: Every item used in the rituals—from bamboo winnowing baskets and clay lamps to banana leaves and seasonal harvest crops—is completely biodegradable, leaving zero environmental waste.
Ancient Epic Roots: Legends link the festival to the Ramayana, where Mata Sita performed the puja in Munger, and the Mahabharata, where Kunti and Draupadi observed it to seek protection and victory for the Pandavas.

✨ Kosi Bharai (also called Kosi Bharna) is a sacred night-time thanksgiving ritual performed during Chhath Puja after a major wish (mannat) is fulfilled. Unlike the regular Chhath rituals, it is observed only by families celebrating milestones such as the birth of a child, recovery from a severe illness, or a marriage.

✨ Meaning and Significance:-
Symbol of Abundance: The word Kosi comes from Kosh, meaning a treasury or storehouse. Performing the ritual expresses gratitude to Chhathi Maiya and Surya Dev while praying that the family's home never lacks prosperity or health.
Optional Vow-Based Tradition: It is not mandatory for every devotee observing Chhath. Families usually take a vow (sankalp) to fill the Kosi once their prayer is answered.

text:
Make 6 Million Antelopes Viral!
 The Great Nile Migration — Earth’s Largest Land Mammal Migration

This is the Great Nile Migration in South Sudan. Roughly 6 million antelope — mainly white-eared kob (~5 million), plus Mongalla gazelle, tiang, and Bohor reedbuck; move across a vast landscape of more than 120,000 km². That is larger than Greece and about the size of Illinois.

A comprehensive 2023 aerial survey (covering 122,774 km² and producing over 330,000 images) confirmed the total at approximately 5.9 million animals (±0.9 million). Later counts have remained stable at around 6 million. This is 2–3 times larger than the famous Serengeti–Mara Great Migration, which involves roughly 1.5–2 million wildebeest, zebra, and gazelle.

Why This Is a Once-in-a-Lifetime Tourist Experience

Imagine standing in one of the last truly wild corners of Africa and watching the landscape fill with living rivers of antelope. Herds can number 100,000 or more. From the air, the plains look like they are moving. On the ground, you experience a level of solitude and rawness that has almost disappeared from East Africa’s more famous parks.

Key attractions for visitors:
• Scale and authenticity — Far fewer vehicles, almost no infrastructure, and landscapes that still feel untouched. You are not sharing the moment with dozens of other safari trucks.
• Aerial spectacle — Flights over the migration reveal its true magnitude in a way ground viewing cannot.
• Complex, multi-directional movement — Unlike the more circular Serengeti route, these antelope follow rains, floods, and seasonal grass in dynamic patterns across wetlands, savannahs, and woodlands. GPS collars have shown individual animals covering nearly 3,000 km in a single year; one tiang logged over 11,500 km in just over three years.
• Cultural connection — The migration is intertwined with the lives of local communities (Dinka, Murle, Anyuak, and others) who have shared this landscape for generations.
• UNESCO recognition — In 2026 the Boma–Badingilo Migratory Landscape became South Sudan’s first UNESCO World Heritage Site, placing the migration on the global stage.

How It Can Transform Tourism in South Sudan

The Serengeti is a world-class, well-developed product with excellent infrastructure and reliable access. The Great Nile Migration offers something different: the chance to help build the next great African safari destination from the ground up.

• Economic opportunity — High-value, low-volume tourism (expedition-style safaris, aerial viewing, community-linked camps) can generate revenue for conservation and local livelihoods in a country that currently has almost no wildlife tourism.
• Conservation incentive — Tourism revenue and international attention create a strong reason to protect migration corridors that currently lie mostly outside formal parks. The animals spend roughly 70% of their time beyond park boundaries.
• Image and identity shift — South Sudan has been known mainly for conflict. A globally recognized migration of this scale, managed in partnership with African Parks and backed by UNESCO status, gives the country a powerful positive story and a reason for the world to invest in its stability and natural heritage.
• Differentiation — While the Serengeti will always be iconic, the Great Nile Migration can position South Sudan as the destination for travelers who want the last great unspoiled terrestrial migration on Earth — larger, wilder, and still largely undiscovered.

The migration survived decades of war and is still there, in extraordinary numbers. With careful, community-centered development, it has the potential to become one of Africa’s defining wildlife experiences — and to rewrite South Sudan’s place in the global tourism map.

📷 Marcus Westberg | National Geographic
