You don't want to miss your daughter's wedding. Like, we're just kind of stuck here. For safety, we just have to deal with it. We just want to get to LA and enjoy our weekend. Blocked in Vegas Airport. ”
So why were planes grounded nationwide?  Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy :e.: “3:36 p.m. we experienced instability for our radar and our communications in our centers and our trachons across the country. So if you don't know this, at airports we have towers, the next rung out is a trachon, after that we have en route centers. The trachons in the centers, we started to have inconsistency in the data from the radars and our communication with uh with airplanes. In other words, blame an overloaded, outdated  air traffic control system. A software update, overwhelmed it.   No indication of anything nefarious like a cyberattack. Airlines, by the way... don't have to give passengers any additional compensation....They do have to offer to rebook a flight or provide full refunds for people who decide to stay home.   College athletes scrambling to get to their destinations in time for games this weekend....Auburn and Purdue players hitting the road on charter busses.”

text:
Titlist Jimmy Carter and challenger Art Aragon meet for the World Lightweight Championship on November 14, 1951, at the Olympic Auditorium in LA.

Aragon had won a non-title 10-round split decision over Carter in August of 1951.

Carter would win a 15-round UD to retain his title.

Flamboyant both in and out of the ring, and "The Golden Boy" long before a guy named De La Hoya was even born, Aragon wore a gold robe and trunks and revelled in playing the villain. Often he would taunt a crowd into booing him, sometimes thumbing his nose at the audience after defeating a popular opponent.
"You ever get booed by 10,000 people? It's exciting," he once said.
He was equally as colorful outside of the ring, golfing with Bob Hope and counting among his friends Marilyn Monroe and William Holden. He was married four times and supposedly had a high-profile romance with actress Mamie Van Doren.
His career, though, was marred by numerous allegations that at least some of his fights were fixed.
In 1956 he was convicted of offering a $500 bribe to welterweight Dick Goldstein to take a dive in a Texas fight, but the conviction was overturned on an appeal.
A sometimes actor, you may recognize him in the Audie Murphy movie, "To Hell and Back," and in John Houston's 'Fat City'.
He finished 90-20-6 with 60 KO's as a pro but this was his only world title fight.

Jimmy Carter would lose and regain the Lightweight title in 1952, to and from Mexico's Lauro Salas. He'll also be one of the very few guys you'll ever read about that fought in a 9-round, yes nine round, scheduled fight. He met  Allan McFater at the Maple Leaf Gardens in a 9-round (he won a UD) fight because the OAC (Ontario Athletic Commission) which would not allow fighters under age 21 to box more than 8 rounds (McFater was under 21).
A world title shot seemed far away when Carter lost his first outing in 1951 to Calvin Smith in Philadelpia and then came the chance to fight the Ike Williams for the world lightweight championship. Williams was only 27 but already had a long, hard career that was beginning to take its toll. He had been an outstanding champion but it was no secret that Williams was also finding it hard to get down to the lightweight limit. Even so, the Williams camp was so confident of victory over carter that they neglected to include the customary return bout clause in the contract. The National Boxing Association thought so little of Carter’s chances that they refused to rank him as a contender.
Little more than 3,000 fans were in Madison Square Garden in May of 1951 to see the title change hands. What the crowd witnessed was a one sided contest as Carter dominated the weight drained champion. Williams was down twice in the fifth round, once in the 10th and again in the 14th as the referee Petey Scalzo, former featherweight champion, signaled the end when the champion went sprawling for a fourth knockdown.
Ike Williams said some years later that his manager, the notorious Blinky Palermo, had offered him $50,000 to lose the fight, with a guarantee that in six months they would fight again with Williams winning. “I should have taken it, but I didn’t” Williams said. “That’s one of the reasons I’m broke now”. 
These types of arrangements were not unusual at the time, the mob had it's hands all over boxing in the 1950's, but there is no evidence that Carter was aware of this. 
Carter was still a hungry fighter after winning the title, and keen to keep himself as busy as possible, since his purse for winning the title was ameasly $1,270. To keep cash coming in he took on a series of non title matches, beating such as Enrique Bolanos, Del Flanagan and Mario Trigo. However that split decision loss against Art Aragon in August 1951 earned the Californian "Golden Boy" this November rematch with Carter’s world title at stake.
From boxrec:
In February Carter outpointed Alan McFater over the unusual distance of nine rounds, and then, in March, he edged a split decision against the number two contender Luther Rawlings. It was anything but the ideal warm up for his title defence less than three weeks later in los Angeles against Lauro Salas.
Salas was an unranked, rugged Mexican brawler and he gave Carter an unexpected tough battle. The champion did not trouble him until the 15th and final round, when Salas was put down for a count of four. The judges were unanimous in Carter’s favor, but Salas had done well enough to earn a rematch which took place in May.
Carter was a 4-1 favorite for the return but after the 24 year old Salas won a split decision Carter accused his opponent of packing the hall with partisan supporters who cheered his every move and swayed the judges into believing that Salas was having more success than he actually was.
A third contest was arranged and the pair met in Chicago, in October. This time Carter took a comfortable verdict to regain the title, but he showed anything but championship form as he won only one of his next four fights, all being non title contests. This did little to encourage confidence in his chance of retaining the title against the hard hitting Tommy Collins whom he faced in the challenger’s hometown of Boston in April 1953.
The fight which was screened live on TV was an appalling mismatch which did serious damage to boxing’s image. The challenger, too brave for his own good, was permitted to absorb one of the worst beatings in title history, while the referee, his own cornermen, commission officials and ringside doctor looked on. Collins was floored seven times in a brutal 3rd round, and the fight should have been stopped after the 3rd knockdown as Collins, his left eye closed, clearly had no idea what was going on.
Collins should never been allowed out for the 4th round, and Carter was obviously unhappy about it. He was reluctant to hit him again and kept looking at the referee Tommy Rawson in the hope that he would call a halt. When he did nothing he knocked the youngster down three more times.Even that was not enough for Rawson who was preparing to order them to box on when Collin’s manager and second at last jumped into the ring to signal their man’s surrender.
Carter’s next defense was against George Arujo in June 1953. Arujo had earned his title shot with wins over Sandy Saddler and paddy De Marco, but had the misfortune of find the erratic Carter on top of his form and the champion stopped him in 13 rounds.
Ever unpredictable Carter lost his next fight, a ten round decision to Johnny Cunningham, a little known welterweight who boxed to supplement his wages as a garbage collector. It was a worrying result for Carter, but he got back in form with two quick non title wins before risking his title again, against Armand Savoie in November 1953.
Like Carter , the Canadian Savoie was a hot and cold fighter whose record was littered with surprising losses mixed in with brilliant victories. For three rounds of his championship challenge it seemed that Savoie was having one of his good nights as he speared Carter with long jabs and stepped in with short hooks to the head. But Carter began to find his range in the fourth and ended the fight with a single, dramatic straight right to the chin in the fifth. Savoie crashed on his back and had only managed to make it to his hands and knees when he was counted out.
Carter opened 1954 with a trip to the Bahamas where he outpointed Billy Lauderdale, before defending in New York City against Paddy De Marco in March. Carter started as a 4-1 favorite, but DeMarco chased him around the ring for 15 rounds and took a unanimous decision as the lethargic champion relied almost exclusively on his left jab.
Carter had a return bout clause in the pre fight contract, but after being originally scheduled for June the fight was twice postponed due to DeMarco injuring an elbow in winning the title, The two men finally met in November 1954. De Marco built up a lead in the first five rounds but from the sixth Carter found his range and raised a swelling on the champs left eye. A left hook floored DeMarco in the ninth, but he rallied to open a cut on Carter’s right eye in the 10th. De Marco was floored twice in the 14th and had nothing left when he came out for the 15th.
The final round lasted just 14 seconds as DeMarco was battered across the ring and the fight was stopped. Carter was champion again for the third time. However the good times were almost over for Carter. 
He began his third reign with a 10 rounds points win over bobby Woods, but was held to a draw by Tony DeMarco (no relation to Paddy) and beaten on a decision by the Cuban Orlando Zulueta. It was all poor preparation for his next defence against Wallace Bud Smith in Boston in June 1955.
Smith, a former USA amateur champion and 1948 Olympic Games semi finalist, was a much improved fighter from the youngster who had lost to Carter in 1950. Carter had the best of the early rounds, but Smith caught him repeatedly with short slashing left hooks in the latter stages to take a split decision. The return fight in Cincinnati ,in October, where 7,000 fans got full value for money, with the outcome in doubt all the way.Smith was just ahead after 12 rounds, having cut Carter’s right eyelid in the 3rd and closed his right eye in the 8th. However the challenger made his big effort in the 13th and pounded the weary Smith around the ring. Smith managed to stay on his feet, even though he had to use the ropes to keep him upright, and then boxed his way out of trouble in the last two rounds to take a unanimous decision.
Carter set about earning another championship chance, but his campaign took a knock when Cisco Andrade took a split decision in his first outing in 1956. Carter came back with a win over Phil Burton, and then had a series of three victories over Don Jordan, Art Aragon and Lauro Salas. When Carter faced 20 year old Larry Boardman in September he was virtually assured of a crack at new champion Joe Brown if he won.
Boardman had beaten Bud Smith and Sandy Sadler in the space of nine weeks, and also held wins over Paddy DeMarco and Frankie Ryff. The youngster proved too lively and ambitious for the veteran and Carter was floored three times before being stopped in the 8th.
He had been down only twice in his whole career, yet he refused to heed the warning signals that he was on the decline and boxed on for another four years. Defeats piled up – 8 in his last 12 fights – before he retired aged 36. 
Carter finished 85-31-9 with 30 KO's.

🇮🇷|Major General Mustapha Izadi Named the Distance. Hundreds of Kilometres. Measure That Against the Chart.

Major General Mustapha Izadi, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps: "America does not dare approach our maritime borders and stays hundreds of kilometres away from them. The world's greatest military power, the United States, is facing declining morale among its aircraft carrier crews. The enemy should learn from the successive defeats it has suffered, or else even greater lessons are on the way. The slightest act of aggression will be met with devastating and painful blows. We target the enemy deep within its positions."

The Distance Is a Chart Measurement

Izadi did not offer a metaphor. Izadi offered a distance.

The Strait of Hormuz narrows to roughly 21 nautical miles across the navigable channel. Iranian territorial waters extend 12 nautical miles from the baseline. The IRGC Navy operates fast attack craft, mine warfare vessels, coastal defence missile batteries, and drone launch sites inside that belt.

An American carrier strike group that stays "hundreds of kilometres away" is staying outside the anti-ship ballistic missile envelope that Iran has displayed. The Khalij Fars, the Hormuz-1 and Hormuz-2, and the Zulfiqar Basir are the anti-ship ballistic systems. The Noor, Qader, and Ghadir are the cruise missile systems. The Fattah-2 and Kheibar Shekan cover the fixed bases.

The carriers are not staying away because they are polite. The carriers are staying away because the weapons that can reach them are deployed on the coast, and the escort architecture has not demonstrated the ability to intercept an anti-ship ballistic missile in terminal phase.

The Morale Claim Has a Ship's Name Behind It

Izadi said the carrier crews are facing declining morale. That is not a slogan. There is a specific ship and a specific withdrawal.

The USS Harry S. Truman was ordered out of the Red Sea after sustaining damage from Ansar Allah missile and drone attacks. The USS Carl Vinson was repositioned. The USS Nimitz was extended and then withdrawn. The Navy's own reporting has documented maintenance backlogs, crew fatigue, and extended deployments across the carrier fleet.

A carrier crew that has been at sea for an extended deployment, that has absorbed drone and missile attacks, that has lost aircraft, and that has watched its escorts burn tankers without being able to stop the enforcement regime is a crew under strain. Izadi named the strain.

The Defeats Izadi Is Counting

The IRGC Deputy Commander-in-Chief said the enemy should learn from the successive defeats. Here is the list, with dates:

56 MQ-9 Reapers downed. Six MQM-170 reconnaissance drones captured intact by electronic warfare over Qeshm. Two LUCAS one-way attack drones destroyed over Bandar Khamir. An MQ-9 downed over Qeshm by the Army's unified air defense network.

Two US aircraft squawking 7700 in a single window. A CMV-22B Osprey off Oman. A second aircraft near Abu Dhabi.

274 US military facilities damaged across seven countries. Estimated losses $15 billion.

The early-warning radar at Jabal Ad-Dukhan in Bahrain destroyed by the IRGC Aerospace Force on 13 November 2026.

Four oil tankers exploded in a single day in the Strait of Hormuz. 11 to 12 anti-ship cruise missiles fired from the Bandar Abbas coast. Eleven-plus tankers burned in nine days. An LPG carrier struck a mine. An oil spill on the Omani coast. Didamar Island's radar, radio, and navigational aids destroyed. The southern route dark.

The elections: the Democratic Party won both chambers. JD Vance published the post-mortem admitting the war lost the election. Donald Trump Jr. endorsed it.

Those are the successive defeats. Izadi is counting them from the IRGC command.

"Deep Within Its Positions" Is the Doctrine Already Published

Izadi's phrase matches the doctrine Major General Ali Abdollahi, Chief of the General Staff and commander of the Khatm al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, published: the response is immediate, impactful, and without geographical limitations.

It matches Sardar Radan, Faraja commander: geography will no longer have meaning, citing the order of Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei.

It matches Brigadier General Esmail Qaani, Quds Force commander: the Resistance is a single front, and the response comes on the surface and deep within.

Four commanders. One phrase. Deep within its positions is not rhetoric. It is the target bank description. The bank includes the bases, the logistics nodes, the sensor architecture, the command centres, and the commercial layer that sustains the force.

The Bahrain radar was deep within the enemy's positions. The Al-Bariqa command room in Yemen that ran mobilisation across four governorates was deep within the enemy's positions. The pumping stations on the East-West Pipeline at Al-Dawadmi, the Madinah region, and Yanbu were deep within the enemy's positions.

The Warning Structure

Izadi's statement has a conditional and a consequence.

The conditional: the slightest act of aggression.

The consequence: devastating and painful blows.

That structure is the same structure in Rezaei's statement: impose a cost that makes aggression expensive and becomes a deterrent. It is the same structure in the Assembly of Experts position paper: the slightest inclination toward surrender squanders the blood of the martyrs and emboldens the enemy. It is the same structure in Makarem Shirazi's ruling: the Quran obligates the preparation of deterrent power.

The condition is set. The consequence is stated. The decision is the enemy's.

The Deployment Context

Izadi spoke on the same day that CENTCOM told Israel and the Gulf states to prepare for the resumption of operations. Three carrier strike groups are in the region. 200 aerial refueling aircraft are deployed. The RC-135U Combat Sent is at RAF Mildenhall, the base used for the June 2025 strikes on Iran's nuclear facilities.

Trump's advisers told him the window closes in January. Netanyahu calls Trump daily. Rubio says sanctions are "very effective." Witkoff and Kushner are at the Kremlin.

Izadi's statement is the ground force tier answering the deployment. The Aerospace Force has the missile city. The Navy has the strait. The Karbala Headquarters in Khuzestan was toured by the Supreme Leader's Representative on 13 November. The Deputy Commander-in-Chief is now stating the distance.

The Bill

Major General Mustapha Izadi, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the IRGC. America does not dare approach the maritime borders. Hundreds of kilometres away. Declining morale among carrier crews. Successive defeats. Greater lessons on the way. Devastating and painful blows for the slightest aggression. Targeting the enemy deep within its positions.

The distance: the Strait of Hormuz at roughly 21 nautical miles. Iranian territorial waters at 12 nautical miles. The anti-ship ballistic and cruise missile envelope on the coast.

The defeats: 56 Reapers, six MQM-170s, two LUCAS, an MQ-9 over Qeshm, two aircraft squawking 7700, 274 facilities damaged, the Bahrain radar destroyed, four tankers in a day, 11 to 12 cruise missiles, eleven-plus tankers burned in nine days, the LPG carrier mined, Didamar's radar destroyed, the southern route dark, the Democratic Party won both chambers, Vance's post-mortem.

The doctrine: immediate, impactful, without geographical limitations from Abdollahi. Geography has no meaning from Radan, citing Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei. Single front, surface and deep within from Qaani. Deep within its positions from Izadi.

The deployment: CENTCOM told Israel and the Gulf to prepare. Three carriers. 200 tankers. The RC-135U at Mildenhall. The January window. Netanyahu's daily calls. Witkoff and Kushner in the Kremlin.

The bill is being paid in a stated distance of hundreds of kilometres, and the receipt is the IRGC Deputy Commander-in-Chief naming the defeats, the morale, the doctrine, and the consequence while the carriers stay outside the envelope and the crews count the days.

TRANSCRIPT
Giving an AI agent checkout authority makes user approval central to shopping. OpenAI says ChatGPT Wallet lets agents select products and complete purchases after people review the items, total and selected card and approve a security check. Payment tokens replace actual card details. The limited rollout covers American ChatGPT Pro users aged eighteen or older with eligible American-issued cards. Some merchants may not support agent checkout; OpenAI says existing eligible card protections and rewards remain.

Voice assistants need current information without making users leave a conversation. Tencent says its Hy Realtime voice model decides from conversational context when to search the web and also supports singing. The company says it is live in Yuanbao voice calls and Tencent Customer Service; Tencent Cloud access is planned soon. These capability claims are company-reported.

Companies using AI agents must decide where execution and session records reside. Anthropic announced self-hosted Claude Managed Agents on November twelve, moving the agent service, sandboxes and stored history onto customer infrastructure. Access must be requested through Anthropic. Model requests still go to Anthropic or another selected provider, so self-hosted agents do not mean local model inference.

Taking notes and tracking action items compete with participating in meetings. ElevenLabs says ElevenAI uses its Scribe speech model for dictation and meeting notes, producing summaries and attendee action items. It also describes live call assistance and notice and consent mechanisms. Introduced November eleven, the experimental workplace app is opening free early access. Its stated functions are company claims, not established workplace outcomes.

Customers often repeat information while staff handle follow-up manually. ElevenLabs announced planned Memory for authenticated returning callers and Routines for tasks such as reminders, waitlist offers and record updates. Its previewed Interaction Engine manages turn-taking, interruptions and model selection. These November eleven announcements remain planned or previewed. The company also plans customer-specific tuning of some open models and voice models in coming months; existing customer records remain primary.

Large voice-agent deployments need model choice and computing capacity. ElevenLabs made NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL available in ElevenAgents in its November eleven partnership expansion. It plans fifteen megawatts of additional Vera Rubin compute alongside existing infrastructure. The integration is live, while the capacity is planned. The partners are also exploring multilingual voice AI on edge computers for industrial machines, robots and vehicles; those are potential applications, not deployed systems.

Patients with only landlines can miss digital appointment reminders. ElevenLabs says its voice AI calls these patients in Poland to remind them about appointments and help reschedule, using NVIDIA infrastructure inside government systems. The company announced this deployment November eleven. It describes on-premises processing of citizen data and audio but provides no measured reduction in missed appointments.

Enterprises often need integration support to put AI agents into service. ElevenLabs launched a partner program, an alliance with McKinsey and QuantumBlack, and a curated marketplace of partner-built AI applications on November eleven. The program includes technical deployment help and certification. Businesses can browse applications and contact partners now. Purchases using existing ElevenLabs commitments are planned for next year, rather than available checkout.

Pests and crop diseases threaten farmers before treatment can begin. Kenya’s Farmerlifeline says solar-powered cameras use AI to detect threats and send local-language text messages with treatment suggestions. Reports describe a fifty-thousand-dollar implementation grant funding six months of field deployment. The checked reports provide no reliability, reach or crop-protection measurements.

Commandos must interpret multiple feeds in complex environments. Britain’s defence ministry says Arondite’s Cobalt uses AI to support faster decisions while unifying sensors, autonomous platforms and operational data. The Royal Navy’s November twelve multi-million-pound deal funds deployment across Commando Force systems, with Norwegian testing planned. The release does not disclose the model, precise contract value or independent performance evaluation.

Whether Chinese AI developers accessed restricted computing hardware has export-control stakes. Will DePue’s November twelve report says numerical patterns in six open-weight models match NVIDIA Blackwell initialization configurations. He reports reproducing some patterns and testing his method against models with disclosed hardware. These are the researcher’s findings; the checked reporting provides no independent replication. Initialization fingerprints do not establish full training hardware, chip location, access arrangements or an export-law violation.

Chinese AI firms may access advanced chips remotely in overseas data centres. The Information reported November eleven that America’s Commerce Department was finalizing restrictions on that access and semiconductor controls covering seven additional countries, including Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand. The anonymously sourced report describes a prospective, unannounced rule. Its final scope and timing remain uncertain; it is not enacted policy.

Engineers balance material use against a structure’s ability to resist forces. An MIT machine-learning copilot suggests regions to thicken or thin while engineers retain editing control. A peer-reviewed study published November ten reports a thirty-nine-percent linear-buckling-load gain over a conventional baseline in one example, with about fifteen seconds of additional total design time. This is a research result, not deployed engineering practice.

Embodied AI needs data and models that connect perception to physical actions. Beijing’s November eleven action plan supports vision-language-action models, world models and reinforcement learning, alongside robot testing and safety-governance capabilities. The plan proposes more than one million hours of high-quality data across at least one hundred scenarios and sets industrial goals for twenty twenty-eight. These are targets, not completed deployments or mandatory safety rules.

Physical-AI developers need ways to train and evaluate systems in simulation. Baidu AI Cloud and Beijing 1011 agreed November twelve to combine cloud computing with physics simulation and physical-AI technology. They plan to explore a platform for simulation-data production, model training and evaluation. The partnership is not evidence that the platform is already operating.

Romanian researchers and institutions need resources to develop AI applications and skills. ICI Bucharest’s director said November twelve that work on Romania AI Factory is underway, including intended applications using confidential data and training people to develop and apply AI. He estimated full readiness in twenty twenty-seven. Those are project aims and an estimate, rather than current availability or demonstrated confidentiality outcomes.

South Africa’s proposed AI centre addresses skills gaps and research capacity. Officials say preparatory work with China is underway and a Chinese technical team is expected to assess the project. The November twelve departmental statement describes a planned talent-development and innovation centre. It gives no opening date or budget, and the centre is not operating.

text:
The CFTC sued its 11th and 12th states in one day as Congress and state courts close in on event contracts

On November 13 the CFTC announced two lawsuits in separate releases. Release 9325-26 covers Arkansas, which the agency calls the 11th state it has sued. Release 9326-26 covers Louisiana, the 12th. The Louisiana release states that the state obtained a court order on Thursday that shut down the operations of more than 30 companies connected to trading CFTC-regulated derivatives, and that the order was issued without notice to the defendants or an opportunity to be heard. The agency also reports amicus briefs in four federal Courts of Appeal and one state Supreme Court.

The two states used different tools, and the difference shows where the pressure on the sector sits. The Arkansas release describes a civil enforcement action in state court against Kalshi, a designated contract market, with penalties that the CFTC says could reach hundreds of millions of dollars. That is a claim against one exchange. The Louisiana order reaches three registration categories at once, since the CFTC's complaint seeks to stop the state from barring event contracts offered by designated contract markets, futures commission merchants and derivatives clearing organizations. A broker that routes customer orders and a clearing house that holds the collateral are inside the order alongside the exchange that lists the contract.

Congress moved on the participant side the same day. The House Oversight Committee's majority staff released a six-page memo on insider trading risk after an inquiry opened on May 22, 2026, and widened on September 29, 2026, to five platforms, namely Kalshi, Polymarket, Hyperliquid Labs, https://t.co/XE6PhZTFPT and PredictIt. The memo states that the committee received nearly 1,700 pages of documents and held five bipartisan briefings. It lists cases that were already public, including an April 24, 2026 indictment alleging more than $409,000 in winnings on Polymarket and CFTC orders of $35,000 on July 31, 2026 and $172,000 on August 28, 2026 over trading on Kalshi. Its recommendation is that Congress consider restricting federal personnel, members and staff from contracts on government actions or political outcomes, whether or not inside information is involved.

The federal perimeter kept expanding while this happened. TokenPost reported that the CFTC registered TLD Clearing, which operates as Backpack Clearing, as a derivatives clearing organization on November 13, with a scope that covers margined futures, fully collateralized futures, futures options and swaps. Its affiliate TLD Markets filed for contract market designation on April 22 and that application is still under review. On-chain venues sit outside this registration track. DefiLlama tracked 141 prediction market protocols on November 14, with Polymarket International holding $326.7 million of locked value and the next largest, Predict Fun, holding $11.4 million.

Three readings will show which side is setting the terms. The first is the CFTC's count of states sued, now 12, and whether a federal court grants or denies interim relief against the Louisiana order before the end of November. The second is whether the Oversight memo turns into a bill with a number in this Congress, as the Senate did for its own members with S. Res. 708 on April 30, 2026. The third is the status of the TLD Markets designation, which determines whether Backpack Clearing has an affiliated exchange to clear for.

🚨 Anthropic, the company behind Claude, makes its stock market debut next Thursday.

And UK retail investors can apply for shares right now.

According to This is Money, demand is so strong that bankers may lift the valuation from $1.3 TRILLION to $1.5 TRILLION.

The numbers:
- Valued at about $183 BILLION as recently as September 2025
- About 312 MILLION monthly users of Claude
- About 1,900 corporate customers each spending over $1 MILLION a year
- 2025 revenue: $4.6 BILLION
- Goldman Sachs forecast for this year: about $52 BILLION
- Forecast for 2030: $600 BILLION

How the retail offer works:
1. About 20% of the shares are set aside for private investors in the US, UK, Australia and Europe
2. The application deadline is Wednesday 18 November, at noon or 1pm depending on the platform
3. The price is set after US markets close on Wednesday
4. If demand is too high, applications get scaled back. In the SpaceX float this summer, only people who asked for up to £2,013 of shares got the full amount

Why this matters:
This is a company valued at over $1 TRILLION, and part of the float is open to UK private investors, not just Wall Street funds.

The cracks:
- Losses are forecast to rise to $40.4 BILLION in 2027 before a profit by 2029
- Big tech is spending about $2 BILLION A DAY on data centres and chips
- OpenAI is said to be aggressively discounting
- Unlike Amazon or Meta, Anthropic has no advertising business to fall back on

One fund manager quoted by This is Money put it bluntly: this is a high-risk bet, and you could lose everything.

The forecasts are huge. So is the gap between today's losses and tomorrow's promised profits.

text:
⚡️ Here is how the proposal works - and why it’s currently hitting a legislative roadblock ahead of Monday’s talks

A proposal spearheaded by Williams Team Principal James Vowles to grant lower-ranked Formula 1 teams a higher spending cap has hit a legislative roadblock, with backing remaining stalled at four teams one month after initial reports by The Race.

The Vowles Proposal and Current StandingsVowles’ initiative aims to help trailing constructors close the performance gap by scaling the cost cap inversely with championship position—the lower a team finishes, the larger the additional spending allowance it receives.
The Supporters: Alongside Williams, the proposal currently has the backing of Cadillac, Alpine, Aston Martin, and Audi.

The Opposition: Haas opposes the measure as it has not yet reached the existing spending ceiling, while Racing Bulls Sporting Director Alan Permane has also expressed disapproval. Top-tier constructors remain firmly against the plan.

To take effect next season, the initiative requires approval from the FIA, FOM, and six of the 11 teams. However, securing support from four teams outside of Williams keeps the door open for a potential 2028 introduction—aligning with preparations for the next major regulation overhaul anticipated in 2030 or 2031.

Growing Momentum Around Staff Salaries and the Cost CapWhile the sliding-scale spending cap remains deadlocked, broader discussions regarding financial rule modifications are gaining traction, driven by concerns over talent retention.

Top teams have raised alarms that the current limits hinder their ability to retain skilled engineers and technicians, who are increasingly drawn to higher-paying roles in the tech sector and rival racing series. Consequently, growing support has emerged for restructuring the cost cap to separate car development expenditures from personnel salaries. Currently, only a team's three highest-paid employees are excluded from the cap.
Mercedes previously advocated for greater flexibility regarding salary expenditure—particularly for junior personnel and early-career specialists—to allow teams to offer more competitive entry-level compensation. Although the FIA ultimately rejected that specific push, Toto Wolff emphasized that the proposal focused strictly on raising employee wages rather than increasing development budgets for car parts.

text:
Singularity Watch, Day 30 — November 14, 2026

The FAA Grounds U.S. Flights and Microsoft 365 Fails Worldwide as Starship Reaches Orbit

Infrastructure: A Nationwide Ground Stop

The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports on November 13 after communication problems hit multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers. The Verge reported the stop was issued at 2:44 PM CST and lifted at 7:15 PM CST, more than four hours later. [1][2]

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the trouble began at 2:36 PM CST, when switches and routers "got overloaded with data" and gave inconsistent radar and communications data. He said radar and communications were never completely lost, and called for $50 billion to modernize the air traffic control system. [3]

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was "zero evidence" so far of a cyberattack or a rogue AI system, without ruling either out, and that patches applied to the existing system sparked the problem. Two airline officials told Reuters the affected network is overseen by L3Harris. [3][2]

By late evening nearly 10,000 flights had been canceled, according to Flightradar24 data cited by Reuters. Reuters called it the longest shutdown since September 11, 2001; the only other nationwide ground stop since then was a 90-minute halt in January 2023. [3]

Ryan quoted a post that asked whether the stop was connected to other recent infrastructure disruptions, and wrote at 6:11 PM CST: "We are now in a perpetual cyber war. Build your defensive agent swarms now." That is his view; officials had found no evidence of an attack. [4][3]

Infrastructure: Microsoft 365 Down Into a Second Day

A global outage of Microsoft 365 email, cloud and AI services that began midday on November 12 was still ongoing on the morning of November 13. Microsoft said servers were failing automated health checks and becoming unavailable, which overloaded the rest, and that it had no evidence of malicious activity. [5]

Some servers became unresponsive again once traffic returned, and Microsoft extended email timeout to 48 hours to preserve delayed mail. Ars Technica reported disruptions to hospitals, banks, courts and government IT in Japan, and Ciaran Martin, former head of the UK's National Cyber Security Centre, told NBC News it looks like one of the biggest outages of all time. [5]

Responding at 4:23 AM CST to a post arguing that AI is too unreliable for mission-critical services, Ryan wrote: "other way around. humans are unreliable and should never be in the loop for mission critical services." [6]

Eric S. Raymond proposed the term "hot-state dependency" for systems that depend on state that cannot be reconstructed after an interruption, and argued for replayable logs of every change. Ryan quoted his definition at 3:00 PM CST and added: "Our society is like this." [7]

Space: Starship Reaches Orbit

Starship Flight 15 lifted off from Starbase, Texas at 4:48 PM CST on November 13 in SpaceX's first attempt to recover both stages at the launch tower. Super Heavy Booster 22 diverted from its planned tower catch and exploded as it came down offshore in the Gulf. [8]

Ship 42 reached orbit and deployed 26 Version 3 Starlink satellites. If systems remain healthy, it is scheduled to return to the launch site for a tower catch about 22.5 hours after launch, around 3:20 PM CST on November 14. [8]

Before launch, Will DePue wrote that a double catch would be one of the most important moments in the history of rocketry, and a SpaceXSI employee who works on Grok Bot wrote that another team was attempting to recover an entire orbital rocket. Ryan surfaced both. [9]

Autonomy: The Cybercab Goes on Sale

Tesla's Robotaxi account announced at 5:27 PM CST that select customers are being invited to buy the Cybercab for personal use. The order page lists $29,990 before taxes, a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, a required $299 monthly Autonomy Subscription with one month included, and estimated delivery in December 2026 in Austin. [10][11]

The two-seat car has no steering wheel or pedals. Electrek reported that it operates only inside Tesla's Robotaxi service areas in five Texas cities and three Florida cities. [10]

Ryan responded twice: "$30k? That's it? How do I get on this list?" and "Add me to the list plz." [11]

Austin's mayor, Kirk Watson, said on November 10 that planners will study extending the city's light rail project about 3 miles to the airport, an analysis expected to take nine to 12 months. Ryan wrote at 10:39 AM CST: "Light rail comes to Austin just as self-driving taxis makes it obsolete." [12]

Compute: Nvidia After Huang

A statement from Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs, dated October 31, recirculated on November 13. It says neither the Singapore Government nor its officials told the Wall Street Journal they were concerned about Alice Huang's ties to Jensen Huang, and that no investigations were conducted in respect of her. It also says investigations into the data center company Megaspeed are ongoing. [13][14]

Brad Gerstner of Altimeter Capital and Gavin Baker of Atreides Management sent a letter to Nvidia's board asking for "a slow, measured, and deliberate process" on future leadership that leaves all options open, "including the potential return of Jensen Huang." The letter says the company will be capably led in the interim by Colette Kress. Ryan surfaced it. [15]

Balaji Srinivasan urged Nvidia employees, shareholders, partners and customers to press the board to reinstate Huang. A Financial Times opinion piece called Huang's fall an indictment of founder mode; Ryan called the post "the ultimate indictment of traditional media." The FT article itself could not be read. [16][17]

Labs: OpenAI Folds Robotics Into General Models

Fortune reported on November 13 that OpenAI has disbanded its stand-alone robotics team, moving robotics research under Chief Research Officer Mark Chen and the applied robotics and hardware teams under President Greg Brockman. OpenAI said robotics remains core to its long-term vision. [18]

OpenAI told Fortune that its general-purpose frontier models, including GPT-6 Astra, have shown they can be applied directly to robotics. Fortune cited an Nvidia study in which an Astra-powered agent reached a 74.8% success rate on a simulated manipulation benchmark, against 51.0% for the best specialized robotic models on that leaderboard. [18]

Andrew Curran wrote that Anthropic reported a similar sudden jump in robotics capability with Fable 5.2, and OpenAI's David Schnurr said robotics at OpenAI is "alive and well," with 15 open roles. Ryan surfaced these posts. [19]

Labs: Anthropic's Compute Dilemma

In interview clips Ryan surfaced, Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei called compute "the deepest business dilemma that the company faces." He said revenue grew roughly 10x in each of 2024 and 2025, while compute has to be bought a year or two ahead. [20]

Amodei said the biggest reason to go public now goes back to these compute bets: more cash gives a bigger buffer between the low-compute and high-compute worlds, so the company can invest in biology, robotics, cybersecurity and knowledge work. [20]

Training: Four Bits From Pretraining Through RL

Thinking Machines Lab published on November 13 how it trained Inkling 2 Small with a native 4-bit NVFP4 forward pass in its expert layers, from the start of pretraining through the final reinforcement learning rollout, on Nvidia GB300 systems. The lab says it is the largest model it knows of trained that way. [21][22]

The recipe gave an 8% wall-clock speedup in pretraining and a 20% speedup in RL over full MXFP8 training, at a cost of about 2% in pretraining compute efficiency. Inkling 2 Small was pretrained in 68 hours on GB300 NVL72 racks, where a similar model took several weeks months earlier. [21]

Agents: Grok Bot Joins Meetings

Grok Bot announced at 1:11 PM CST that it can now join meetings to answer questions, take on work and track team decisions. Sam Sokolin said Grok Bot harness optimizations shipped this week give about 7% more usage per plan and up to about 15% more on routine runs. A separate post reported that SpaceXSI is working on an unannounced "Bot Factory" that chains bots in a fixed order. [23]

The Information reported, in an article that could not be read but was summarized by https://t.co/GPC7zcWbsm, that SpaceX's AI group laid off about 60 employees working on Grok Imagine, its image and video generator, leaving a handful to maintain it as the company prioritizes AI coding tools and Grok Bot. Ryan wrote: "Imagine is cool. But coding is far, far more valuable." [24][25]

Ryan also wrote, "Don't be locked into one harness or model. Use all of them. Own your own workflows," and praised a developer's self-hosted agent app, Seneca, which its author said will be released under the MIT license next week. He surfaced a creator's Grok Bot video editing workflow that runs five stages on its own. [26]

Security: Hardware Isolation and Open Weights

Apple Security Research published Secure Exclaves on November 12: protected runtimes that process camera and microphone data apart from the rest of the system, so the main operating system, apps and Apple cannot access it. Apple said it will keep hardening the system with AI-accelerated vulnerability research and expanded formal verification. Ryan surfaced the post. [27][28]

Transformer reported that more than 6,500 models tagged abliterated, uncensored or heretic were on Hugging Face in July, and that Hugging Face removed one model marketed for offensive cyber use. An uploader of such models responded that abliteration only removes refusals, and that their Qwen3.8 Flash-Next model had about 358,000 downloads in 30 days. [29][30]

CodeRabbit said its Deep Scans of 1,125 public repositories produced 1,215 high or critical findings, 75 of them already fixed. Ryan also surfaced a post citing 61 working bug reproductions on a benchmark, quoting the launch of Breken, which tests systems against synthetic users, agents and failing services. [31][32]

Engineering: Software That Repairs Itself

Ryan's one original post of the day, at 7:28 AM CST, read "self-healing software is real." It showed an agent report of a near miss in which two sessions updated the same checkout, and an issue it filed for one safe update command that gives no reset advice. [33]

Work: Leverage

In a morning exchange about developers who say they no longer like their jobs because of AI, Ryan wrote that AI "is leverage for your mind" and "far more powerful than hand coding," and that "the goal is to solve more problems better, faster, cheaper." He endorsed a reply saying that with a good codebase and verification loop, Opus 5.5 writes better code than its author. [34]

Ryan wrote that a bot "will be the primary user interface for a computer moving foward," and answered a post saying there is more to life than shipping with "No there isn't. Keep shipping." [35]

Lenny Rachitsky reported that 15% of open tech roles are now in the Bay Area, a record, while just 14% offer a remote option, the lowest on record. Ryan surfaced the post. [36]

Medicine and Commerce

Ryan surfaced an interview in which Isomorphic Labs president Max Jaderberg described using AI to choose 20 or 50 molecules to test instead of screening hundreds of thousands. He also surfaced a post reporting that Shopify fine-tuned Qwen3-32B for its commerce assistant and found it 2.2 times faster and 68% cheaper than the closed model it replaced. [37]

This Record

Day 29 of this record was published on @AstrohackerLabs at 4:28 AM CST on November 13. The account's other activity in this window was plain reposts of Ryan's posts. [38]

text:
WHEN YOUR FRIEND BECOMES THE FAMILY TECH SUPPORT 😂😭
Something happened at my friend's house in Lagos last Sunday.
I went to visit Chuka, and his younger sister was struggling with her new phone. She couldn't transfer her WhatsApp messages from her old phone.
Chuka told her, "Give it to me. I'll sort it out."
Omo, that was the beginning of his suffering. 😂
Within 20 minutes, his mother brought her phone.
"Since you're already doing something, help me check why my WhatsApp pictures are not showing in my gallery."
Before he could finish, his father came out with his phone.
"Chuka, this phone keeps showing me adverts. I think somebody is monitoring me."
His younger brother followed.
"Bro, please help me recover my Gmail password."
I was just sitting there watching a full IT department emerge in one sitting.
The funniest part was when his aunt called from Ibadan.
"Chuka, I heard you understand these phones. Please, I want to know how to make my Facebook videos go viral."
He hadn't even responded when his mother shouted from the kitchen:
"Please don't forget to fix the television remote too!"
I burst out laughing.
Chuka looked at me and said:
"Guy, I studied Computer Science for four years. I have worked in tech for six years. Yet nobody in this family has ever asked me how my career is going. But once their phone develops a problem, everybody remembers my name." 😭😂
I told him to start charging consultation fees.
He said he tried that once, and his mother told him he had changed since he started earning money.
Now, here's my question:
Should people who have a particular skill be expected to offer free services to family and friends, or is it perfectly reasonable to charge them just like any other customer?
Let's hear both sides. 😂

text:
Sometimes people accuse me of being a grifter or trying to squeeze every possible dollar out of my audience. 

Honestly, it hurts because that’s never been my motivation.  We’re living through an AI gold rush. Startups are raising millions, and having an audience in tech creates enormous opportunities to make money.

 I regularly turn down offers from companies willing to pay thousands of dollars for a single promotional tweet.
I could make a fortune doing sponsored posts, but I’ve always believed that my opinions should never be for sale.

  The truth is, money is no longer my main motivation. Building products, experimenting with ideas, and seeing people use something I’ve created bring me far more satisfaction. 

 Making money from my apps is still exciting, not because I need more money, but because someone choosing to pay for something I built tells me that I’ve created real value. 

 For years, I worked alone, building apps without many people around me who shared the same interests. Today, I’ve found a community of like-minded builders, achieved financial freedom, and get to spend my time doing what I genuinely enjoy. 

 I don't want to chase money endlessly. I want to keep building interesting things, experimenting, learning, and working alongside people who share the same passion.

text:
MIT Technology Review’s What’s Next series looks across industries, trends, and technologies to give you a first look at the future. You can read the rest of our series here.

In 2023, it almost felt as if the promise of robotaxis was soon to be fulfilled. Hailing a robotaxi had briefly become the new trendy thing to do in San Francisco, as simple and everyday as ordering a delivery via app. However, that dream crashed and burned in October, when a serious accident in downtown San Francisco involving a vehicle belonging to Cruise, one of the leading US robotaxi companies, ignited distrust, casting a long shadow over the technology’s future. 

Following that and another accident, the state of California suspended Cruise’s operations there indefinitely, and the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration launched an investigation of the company. Since then, Cruise has pulled all its vehicles from the road and laid off 24% of its workforce.

Despite that, other robotaxi companies are still forging ahead. In half a dozen cities in the US and China, fleets of robotaxis run by companies such as Waymo and Baidu are still serving anyone who would like to try them. Regulators in places like San Francisco, Phoenix, Beijing, and Shanghai now allow these vehicles to drive without human safety operators. 

However, other perils loom. Robotaxi companies need to make a return on the vast sums that have been invested into getting them up and running. Until robotaxis become cheaper, they can’t meaningfully compete with conventional taxis and Uber. Yet at the same time, if companies try to increase adoption too fast, they risk following in Cruise’s footsteps. Waymo, another major robotaxi operator, has been going more slowly and cautiously. But no one is immune to accidents. 

“If they have an accident, it’s going to be big news, and it will hurt everyone,” says Missy Cummings, a professor and director of the Mason Autonomy and Robotics Center at George Mason University. “That’s the big lesson of this year. The whole industry is on thin ice.”

MIT Technology Review talked to experts about how to understand the challenges facing the robotaxi industry. Here’s how they expect it to change in 2024.

Money, money, money

After years of testing robotaxis on the road, companies have demonstrated that a version of the autonomous driving technology is ready today, though with some heavy asterisks. They operate only within strict, pre-set geographical boundaries; while some cars no longer have a human operator in the driver’s seat, they still require remote operators to take control in case of emergencies; and they are limited to warmer climates, because snow can be challenging for the cars’ cameras and sensors. 

“From what has been disclosed publicly, these systems still rely on some remote human supervision to operate safely. This is why I am calling them automated rather than autonomous,” says Ramanarayan Vasudevan, an associate professor of robotics and mechanical engineering at the University of Michigan.

The problem is that this version of automated driving is much more costly than traditional taxis. A robotaxi ride can be “several orders of magnitude more expensive than what it costs other taxi companies,” he says. “Unfortunately I don’t think the technology will dramatically change in the coming year to really drive down that cost.”

That higher ticket price will inevitably suppress demand. If robotaxis want to keep customers—not just those curious to try it out for the first time—they need to make the service cheaper than other forms of transportation. 

Bryant Walker Smith, an associate professor of law at the University of South Carolina, echoes this concern. “These companies are competing with an Uber driver who, in any estimate, makes less than minimum wage, has a midpriced car, and probably maintains it themselves,” he says. 

By way of contrast, robotaxis are expensive vehicles packed full of cameras, sensors, and advanced software systems, and they require constant monitoring and help from humans. It’s almost impossible for them to compete with ride-sharing services yet, at least until a lot more robotaxis can hit the road.

And as robotaxi companies keep burning the cash from investors, concerns are growing that they are not getting enough in return for their vast expenditure, says Smith. That means even more pressure to produce results, while balancing the potential revenues and costs. 

The resistance to scaling up

In the US, there are currently four cities where people can take a robotaxi: San Francisco, Phoenix, Los Angeles, and Las Vegas. 

The terms differ by city. Some require you to sign up for a waitlist first, which could take months to clear, while others only operate the vehicles in a small area.

Expanding robotaxi services into a new city involves a huge upfront effort and cost: the new area has to be thoroughly mapped (and that map has to be kept up to date), and the operator has to buy more autonomous vehicles to keep up with demand. 

Also, cars whose autonomous systems are geared toward, say, San Francisco have a limited ability to adapt to Austin, says Cummings, who’s researching how to measure this type of adaptability. “If I’m looking at that as a basic research question, it probably means the companies haven’t learned something important yet,” she says. 

These factors have combined to cause renewed concern about robotaxis’ profitability. Even after Cruise removed its vehicles from the road, Waymo, the other major robotaxi company in the US, hasn’t jumped in to fill the vacuum. Since each robotaxi ride currently costs the company more money than it makes, there’s hardly an appetite for endless expansion.

Worldwide development

It’s not just the US where robotaxis are being researched, tested, and even deployed. 

China is the other leader right now, and it is proceeding on roughly the same timeline as the US. In 2023, a few cities in China, including Beijing and Shanghai, received government clearance to run robotaxies on the road without any safety operators. However, the cars can only run in certain small and relatively remote areas of the cities, making the service tricky to access for most people.

The Middle East is also quickly gaining a foothold in the sector, with the help of Chinese and American companies. Saudi Arabia invested $100 million in the Chinese robotaxi startup https://t.co/t10RuzrjO1 to bring its cars to Neom, a futuristic city it’s constructing that will supposedly be built with all the latest technologies. Meanwhile, Dubai and Abu Dhabi are competing with each other to become the first city in the Middle East to pilot driverless vehicles on the road, with vehicles made by Cruise and the Chinese company WeRide.

Chinese robotaxi companies face the same central challenge as their US peers: proving their profitability. A push to monetize permeated the Chinese industry in 2023 and launched a new trend: Chinese self-driving companies are now racing to sell their autopilot systems to other companies. This lets them make some quick cash by repackaging their technologies into less advanced but more in-demand services, like urban autopilot systems that can be sold to carmakers.

Meanwhile, robotaxi development in Europe has lagged behind, partly because countries there prefer deploying autonomous vehicles in mass transit. While Germany, the UK, and France have seen robotaxis running road tests, commercial operations remain a distant hope. 

Lessons from Cruise’s fiasco

Cruise’s dreadful experience points to one major remaining roadblock for robotaxis: they still sometimes behave erratically. When a human driver (in a non-autonomous vehicle) hit a pedestrian in San Francisco in October and drove away from the scene, a passing Cruise car then ran over the victim and dragged her 20 feet before stopping. 

“We are deeply concerned that more people will be killed, more first responders will be obstructed, more sudden stops will happen,” says Cathy Chase, president of Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety, an activist group based in Washington, DC. “We are not against autonomous vehicles. We are concerned about the unsafe deployment and a rush to the market at the expense of the traveling public.”

These companies are simply not reporting enough data to show us how safe their vehicles are, she says. While they are required to submit data to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the data is heavily redacted in the name of protecting trade secrets before it’s released to the public. Some federal bills proposed in the last year, which haven’t passed, could even lighten these reporting requirements, Chase says.

“If there’s a silver lining in this accident, it’s that people were forced to reckon with the fact that these operations are not simple and not that straightforward,” Cummings says. It will likely cause the industry to rely more on remote human operators, something that could have changed the Cruise vehicle’s response in the October accident. But introducing more humans will further tip the balance away from profitability.

Meanwhile, Cruise was accused by the California Public Utilities Commission of misleading the public and regulators about its involvement in the incident. “If we cannot trust these companies, then they have no businesses on our roads,” says Smith. 

A Cruise spokesperson told MIT Technology Review the company has no updates to share currently but pointed to a blog post from November saying it had hired third-party law firms and technology consultants to review the accident and Cruise’s responses to the regulators. In a settlement proposal to CPUC, Cruise also offered to share more data, including “collision reporting as well as regular reports detailing incidents involving stopped AVs.”

The future of Cruise remains unclear, and so does the company’s original plan to launch operations in several more cities soon. Meanwhile, though, Waymo is applying to expand its services in Los Angeles while taking its vehicles to the highways of Phoenix. Zoox, an autonomous-driving startup owned by Amazon, could launch commercial service in Las Vegas this year. For residents of these cities, more and more robotaxis may be on the road in 2024.

Correction: The story has been updated to clarify that Cruise’s October 2 accident was not fatal. The victim was hospitalized with serious injuries but survived.

Civil Twilight:  
Begins in the morning, or ends in the evening, when the geometric center of the SUN is 6 degrees below the horizon.  Therefore morning civil twilight begins when the geometric center of the sun is 6 degrees below the horizon, and ends at sunrise.  Evening civil twilight begins at sunset, and ends when the geometric center of the sun is 6 degrees below the horizon.  Under these conditions absent fog or other restrictions, the brightest stars and planets can be seen, the horizon and terrestrial objects can be discerned, and in many cases, artificial lighting is not needed. Civil Twilight is also known as Civil Dawn and Civil Dusk.
Nautical Twilight:
Begins in the morning, or ends in the evening, when the geometric center of the sun is 12 degrees below the horizon.  In general, the term nautical twilight refers to sailors being able to take reliable readings via well known stars because the horizon is still visible, even under moonless conditions.  Absent fog or other restrictions, outlines of terrestrial objects may still be discernible, but detailed outdoor activities are likely curtailed without artificial illumination. Nautical Twilight is also known as Nautical Dawn and Nautical Dusk.
Astronomical Twilight:
Begins in the morning, or ends in the evening, when the geometric center of the sun is 18 degrees below the horizon.  In astronomical twilight, sky illumination is so faint that most casual observers would regard the sky as fully dark, especially under urban or suburban light pollution.  Under astronomical twilight, the horizon is not discernible and moderately faint stars or planets can be observed with the naked eye under a non light polluted sky.  But to test the limits of naked eye observations, the sun needs to be more than 18 degrees below the horizon.  Point light sources such as stars and planets can be readily studied by astronomers under astronomical twilight.  But diffuse light sources such as galaxies, nebula, and globular clusters need to be observed under a totally dark sky, again when the sun is more than 18 degrees below the horizon.

Britain used chemical weapons on Russia, and Winston Churchill was the man who offered them.

It was right after World War I, while British troops were fighting in Russia's Civil War. They dropped M Devices from aircraft, bombs that released an arsenic-based toxic smoke. Churchill, then Britain's Secretary of State for War and Air, offered the weapon to General Ironside, and the air attacks began around Emtsa, a village in northern Russia.

Nine days after one bombing, a British officer found civilians in Emtsa with signs of chemical exposure. Prisoners described men lying on the ground bleeding from the nose and mouth, and British army doctors examined 46 gassed prisoners.

London was pleased. General Rawlinson credited the success of the Arkhangelsk operations largely to the M Bombs, and Ironside praised their effect on the enemy's morale. When the British finally pulled out, they dumped around 47,000 unused devices into the White Sea. All of it is in British military records.

text:
You built a business before entering politics. You produced something people chose to buy. That gives me some hope that you understand the difference between creating value and organising an expensive conference about the possibility of creating value.

I am asking you to call out the arrogance, waste and theatrical self importance that have become so exhausting in public life. 

This criticism applies across political parties. The ANC, DA, EFF, MK and every other party should face the same scrutiny. ActionSA must be included. Political loyalty should never oblige a citizen to applaud nonsense.

We are forever “going forwards.”

Going forwards to where? The next conference venue? The next five star lunch? Another dinner at which everyone solemnly agrees that further engagement is required?

The country is apparently going forwards while the waistline goes sideways.

Implementation remains uncertain. Lunch arrives punctually.

“His Excellency.” “The Honourable Member.” “Distinguished delegates.” “Esteemed colleagues.”

What an extraordinary amount of verbal polishing these people require.

Excellence should be evident in the work. Honour should be evident in the conduct. Yet parliamentary proceedings have included physical confrontations and violence, documented in Parliament’s own records. The titles become a rather expensive joke when the distinguished gentlemen need separating.

And let us dispense with the fantasy that office confers a superior category of human existence. After his lavish lunch, His Excellency sits on the toilet like everyone else. His digestive system has never read the protocol manual.

The same titles accomplish even less in the grave. A funeral programme may list twenty distinctions; mortality does not offer an executive exemption.

What matters is what a person did for the living.

Yet the machinery of government can become remarkably energetic when arranging honours for the dead. A parliamentary reply reported in 2020 disclosed R105.6 million spent on fifteen official funerals between February 2018 and February 2020. Those are historical figures, but they illustrate the scale that ceremonial spending can reach.

Honour the dead with dignity and restraint. Then show comparable urgency towards the pensioner trying to remain in her home, the hungry child and the household waiting for clean water.

A grand funeral cannot compensate for a neglected life.

When officials indulge in avoidable luxury while people struggle for food and shelter, I regard that as a form of moral treason, a betrayal of the public trust. The people whose labour sustains government should never become an inconvenience between courses.

Then there is the jargon.

“Strategic alignment.” “Institutional strengthening.” “Stakeholder engagement.” “Catalytic interventions.” “Implementation modalities.” “Unlocking synergies.” “An integrated roadmap.”

One can almost hear the announcement:

“The Distinguished Executive Keystone Round Table Subcommittee on Strategic Pipeline Coordination has resolved to establish a Cabinet Steering Mechanism to facilitate preliminary stakeholder engagement concerning the implementation framework for the way forward.”

A magnificent sentence. Nobody has repaired the pipe.

By the time the deputy chairperson has finished thanking the chairperson for recognising the deputy chairperson, the caterers have achieved the only measurable delivery target.

We hear about Cabinets, chairs, benches and round tables. After the Phala Phala controversy over foreign currency reportedly concealed in a sofa, even the upholstery acquired national political significance. South Africans could be forgiven for wanting less attention paid to the furniture and more to the people outside the room.

When a photograph shows a hundred officials assembled in a conference venue, publish the full bill underneath it. Flights, hotels, transport, security, catering, consultants and staff time. Explain why each person attended and what the gathering accomplished.

If the cost runs into millions, say so. Then explain its value to someone choosing between groceries and electricity.

A group photograph proves that people arrived. It does not prove that they governed.

Put routine meetings online. Circulate documents. Record decisions. Allocate responsibility. Set deadlines. Anyone proposing an expensive gathering should explain why the work requires it.

For perspective, the 2026/27 national budget allocates approximately R2.46 billion to VIP Protection Services alone. Expenditure on protection requires justification, and ordinary people are entitled to demand equal seriousness about their safety.

Cape Town deserves the same scrutiny as every other administration.

Consider the pensioner who bought a modest house decades ago, paid the bond, maintained the property and expected some security in retirement. The neighbourhood becomes more expensive. The valuation increases. The pensioner has sold nothing, received no windfall and gained no additional monthly income.

A valuation notice cannot buy groceries.

Property rates based on market value are authorised under national legislation. But that does not settle the question of affordability. A home can become more valuable while its owner becomes less able to meet monthly extortion bills. It is a thieving scam. Authorized theft really. 

Cape Town residents are being driven to sell because of rising rates and neighbourhood costs. Reporting from Woodstock and Salt River documented such accounts in 2017; more recent reporting records homeowners warning that higher municipal bills could force them out. These concerns should be investigated and measured, rather than dismissed as resistance to paying.

A person does not have to be physically evicted to be forced out economically. A sale may look voluntary on a transfer document while being the only remaining escape from extortion bills the owner cannot meet.

That distinction matters to the family packing its belongings.

Relief should be accessible, predictable and processed promptly. An elderly person should not need the administrative stamina of a tender consultant to obtain assistance. Its all more extortion upon extortion. An army of parasites. People just want to be left alone in old age. 

Unpaid municipal "debt" can ultimately lead to legal proceedings and a court authorised sale of property. A primary residence requires judicial scrutiny, including consideration of alternatives, but the risk of losing it is real. Courts are not clean either. So many examples of crooked judges. 

Paying off the bank should not be followed by permanent anxiety about whether municipal demands will make remaining in the home impossible.

And how does the VP afford to live in multiple mansions and pay all these rates based on his salary? What business did he start?

Against that background, spending priorities deserve relentless examination. Cape Town reported budgets of approximately R9.39 million for a synthetic pitch in Site B and R9.68 million for the synthetic pitch installation phase at Delft. Who gets the tenders for all this plastic crap? Why not build libraries and computer centres instead? 

When residents struggle to remain in their homes, officials must be prepared to defend the priority given to plastic playing surfaces. Publish the contractors, beneficial owners, competing bids, final expenditure, maintenance obligations and actual use.

Compare that expenditure with computer centres, workshop equipment, libraries, agricultural training and repairs to existing facilities. Explain the benefits in terms residents can inspect.

A pensioner cannot pay a municipal account with a photograph of a councillor opening a football field.

There is also a concrete legal record to confront. On 30 April 2026, the Western Cape High Court declared three Cape Town charges unlawful and invalid: the citywide cleaning charge and fixed water and sewerage charges calculated through property value bands. The order took effect at the end of June. It concerned those particular charges, rather than the general legality of property rates.

Residents should not have to fund litigation to establish the limits of powers exercised by an administration they already pay for.

Now consider executive remuneration.

Cape Town’s audited 2024/25 statements disclose annual remuneration of approximately R4.745 million for the city manager, R3.888 million for the finance executive and R3.756 million for the corporate services executive. Divided by twelve, those totals are approximately R395,000, R324,000 and R313,000 a month, including bonuses, contributions and other disclosed items.

Those figures demand an exceptionally convincing account of value.

Before another pensioner is told to tighten her belt, let the administration demonstrate restraint in its own expenditure. The instruction loses some authority when delivered from a particularly comfortable chair.

The same standard belongs at national level. Publish verified qualifications, relevant experience, performance records and the reasons for appointments. Winning an election does not confer engineering knowledge. Party seniority does not establish financial competence.

Anyone who has studied government should be especially embarrassed to govern badly.

Where political wealth cannot be reconciled with legitimate income, investigate it independently. What business produced the money? What investment generated the return? What financed the properties? What interests are held through companies or associates?

Recover stolen money and prosecute proven corruption. Party membership must provide no protection.

These are questions about human decisions and accountability. We need no supernatural explanation for greed or indifference.

Taxation itself deserves a more honest moral discussion.

For a working person, money often represents hours of finite life. A shift completed, a field planted, a machine repaired, a patient treated or a product manufactured. Behind the accounting entry stands somebody’s effort.

When public money is wasted, some of that effort has been wasted with it.

The monetary system can create banknotes and electronic balances. It cannot create food, houses, skilled labour or additional years of human life merely by entering numbers into a computer. Money creation also has economic consequences, including inflation risks.

Every public expense should therefore face a plain question: what useful result justifies taking this portion of someone else’s working life?

A functioning water system can answer. An effective emergency service can answer. An unnecessary entourage and another ceremonial dinner deserve a much more hostile examination.

Young people need credible reasons to believe that decades of work and saving can produce security. They deserve affordable routes into housing, useful education and honest retirement arrangements.

That does not justify predicting that every pension will collapse. It demands protection of savings, transparent fees and risks, and serious attention to purchasing power.

The two pot system did not itself slash existing pensioners’ payments. It allows eligible active members access to a savings component while preserving another component for retirement. The concern is what happens when financial distress repeatedly drives people to consume money intended for later life.

A country should be ashamed when retirement becomes an exercise in deciding which essential bill can remain unpaid.

Meanwhile, ordinary people face unreliable water, sewage pollution, violent crime, gangs, extortion, unemployment, infrastructure theft, deteriorating roads, housing shortages and pressure on clinics and public transport.

In June 2026, Parliament reported that 47% of wastewater systems were in a critical state. That calls for trained people, maintained equipment and competent management. An executive luncheon cannot disinfect sewage.

Our cities should be safe, clean and governed. Drug trafficking requires intelligence, evidence, arrests, prosecution, asset recovery and action against corrupt protectors. Nationality should provide neither immunity nor a substitute for evidence.

The army has already been deployed in support of SAPS against gangsterism and illegal mining, with 2,200 personnel authorised from March 2026 to March 2027. The public should be shown what lasting results that deployment produces.

Secure the borders. Enforce lawful entry requirements. Prosecute officials who sell access. Set immigration policy against demonstrated capacity in employment, housing and services, while maintaining lawful asylum procedures.

Education should be the foundation of rebuilding that capacity.

I mean education for every child, of every race, in wealthy suburbs, townships, rural villages and informal settlements. Practical competence must never become a lesser track reserved for poor children.

Teach strong literacy, mathematics, science and digital skills. Work towards proficiency in three languages. Equip schools with workshops, computer centres, libraries and productive gardens.

By eighteen, learners should have encountered at least ten credible occupational pathways: crop production, plumbing, electrical installation, welding, carpentry, bricklaying, road construction, motor mechanics, refrigeration and electronics repair.

Give them useful foundations and clear routes into apprenticeships and specialised training. Where two years is sufficient, make it accessible. Where longer training or certification is required, provide a proper route.

Let children grow potatoes, mielies and vegetables. Teach soil, irrigation, harvesting, storage and costing. Give them supervised experience with tools, pumps, pipes, construction and electrical principles.

Literature can enrich a life. Practical competence helps sustain one. No learner should leave years of schooling unable to read confidently, calculate accurately or identify a realistic route into useful work.

The objective should be a generation capable of doing more than completing applications and waiting.

Mr Mashaba, I am asking you to confront the documented failures plainly. The financial statements, court judgments and public reports can be examined. The satire should never become an excuse for avoiding the substance.

Apply the same standard inside your own party.

Apartheid institutionalised racial oppression. Present leaders must answer for their own conduct. No political history, skin colour or party emblem confers permanent immunity from criticism.

People of every race have a common interest in opposing corruption, arrogance and the misuse of their labour and trust.

The country needs fundamental changes in appointments, spending, accountability and education. Another slogan will not suffice. Neither will another photograph of well fed officials applauding a declaration of their intention to become more concerned.

I regard that performance as clowning because it substitutes ceremony for competence and demands reverence for the substitution.

The tragedy is that people can lose years, savings and homes while the performance continues.

Honour the dead with restraint. Serve the living with urgency.

Let “excellent” describe the work and “honourable” describe the conduct.

And before the next committee goes forwards to lunch, require it to explain what it has actually done.
